job.title: Shift Engineer (Electrical)
job.description:
Responsibilities

1\. Lead operations and maintenance on assigned shift and monitor performance of assigned responsibilities. Perform service requests, repair and/or troubleshoot ensuring that work performed in critical environment is accomplished efficiently with a minimum amount of disruption and inconvenience to customer. Followed up with clean up and subsequent inspection to ensure continuous trouble-free operation. Check malfunctioning equipment and ascertains corrective action required to restore to satisfactory operating condition. 2\. Responsible for the daily operation, maintenance, and inspections of assigned critical environment systems, which may include the following: mechanical, electrical, cabling, fire detection and suppression, life safety, lighting, temperature control systems, building management systems, and digital systems. 3\. Responsible to inspect and examine prior sign off the maintained equipment/system done by maintenance vendor or OEM vendor witness by technician. Ensure vendor follows closely to the maintenance work method statement without deviation and sign off for each work step. Should abnormality occur, Engineer should call for work halt and escalate to monitoring centre and seek for Lead Engineer work clearance prior proceed to perform troubleshoot and/or investigation. 4\. Routinely performs all work in strict accordance with governing Change Control Application Process, standard operating procedures, and maintenance work instructions. 5\. Leads or directly operates and monitors critical system equipment and components. Oversees Change Control Application Process work efforts (including 3rd party contractors) for the safe and compliant operation, maintenance (corrective and preventive), and modification of critical equipment. Disables and enables fire alarm control panels and systems. 6\. Provides on-the-job training and technical support to junior engineer and technicians. 7\. Support implementation of the preventative maintenance program for their assigned shift. Specific duties include but are not limited to: scheduling of preventative maintenance with a minimum disruption of building services, performing and/or supervise preventative maintenance tasks, orders parts and equipment required for repair, maintenance and installation of new equipment and facilities, and maintains inventory. 8\. Responsible for the operations of monitoring center, which is the nerve centre of the Data Centre, involving rotate with other shift engineer to ensure building management system is continuously man, handling of incident management (work includes escalation, reporting, investigation, conduct root caused analysis, remediation/rectification through incident closure) and work order management. Respond immediately to emergency situations and customer concerns. 9\. Deliver all tasks for customer’s service level agreement are in compliance at all time, the SLA covers such as incident escalate to customer within 15 minutes upon reported to monitoring centre, written incident report issue within 24 hours, etc. 10\. Receives work order for Preventative and Corrective maintenance on critical systems. Consult superior and staff as appropriate to identify and order necessary materials to complete all maintenance and perform necessary work. Finalize work orders by completing necessary documentation. 11\. Develops construction and maintenance Change Control Application. Implementations or ensure implementations of Change Control Application or work method statement including LOTO (log out/tag out) required under Change Management Work Flow Process for assigned facilities and systems. 12\. Performs all work safely in accordance with the governing Safety Program. Comply with company policy and local law for the safe storage, usage, and disposal of hazardous materials. Maintains a clean and safe workplace. 13\. Implement to SOP and ERP and have in depth understanding of the critical system/facilities. 14\. Update tools and supply inventories as appropriate. Specific duties include, but not limited to preparing and submitting purchase-order requests, developing sources for stock materials and performing periodic checks for supplies. 15\. Identify safety hazards within the critical environment, report to Security & Safety Office or superior. Ensure that our coworkers and customers work in a safe environment. Work safety is a key area of focus, staff should put on proper PPE while carrying out their works and comply with safety work rules. 16\. Ensure that compliance of all regulatory laws and guidelines are met as they relate to the operation of the building’s infrastructure and including work deliveries. Responsible for alerting your reporting manager or senior management of any discrepancies. 17\. Lead the team to identify occupational hazards and risks, and ensure effective risk control. 18\. Maintain effectiveness of the ISO9001, ISO14001 & ISO45001 Quality Environment, Health and Safety Management System.

Qualifications

1\. Proficient in English through all mediums of communication. Ability to write and review good quality detailed work scripts, methods of procedure, and standard operating procedures. Prepare incident report. 2\. Good knowledge of all laws that govern building management and maintenance, including building safety, emergency evacuation and environment protection. 3\. Professional Engineering Diploma in an Engineering field (Mechanical or Electrical) with min. 4-6 years of relevant work experience in Data Centre environment or Hi-tech factory/plant (e.g. semi-conductor). Candidate with other professional certificate has advantage OR Bachelor of Science degree in an Engineering field with min. 1-3 years relevant work experience in Data Centre environment or Hi-tech factory/plant (e.g. semi-conductor). 4\. For Electrical Engineer, a valid Electrical switching certificate and/or license (Chargeman) for LV/HT electrical system is preferred. 5\. Some technical knowledge with hands on knowledge/experience and understanding of critical data center systems, including HVAC, Standby emergency power, uninterruptible power supplies, and associated infrastructure. 6\. Proficient in computer applications and software, including commercial computerized maintenance management systems, Microsoft Word, PowerPoint, and Excel.

job.title: Manager, Solution Architecture
job.description:
Job Description

Position Title: Manager, Solution Architecture (DRIL)

Location: Singapore

Your role

At Digital Realty, we're building the next generation of AI-ready infrastructure. We're looking for a Senior Solutions Architect to join our Digital Realty Innovation Lab (DRIL), where new ideas are transformed into practical solutions for our customers and our business.

This role combines architecture, engineering, and innovation. You'll help design modern infrastructure that supports AI, cloud, and enterprise workloads while collaborating with experts across engineering, operations, and facilities.

We're looking for someone with strong infrastructure experience who enjoys solving complex technical challenges, learning new technologies, and working with cross-functional teams. You don't need to have experience with every technology listed below—we value curiosity, adaptability, and a willingness to learn.

What you’ll do

Design Modern Infrastructure

  • Design scalable infrastructure solutions for enterprise, hybrid cloud, and AI workloads.
  • Create architectures that balance performance, reliability, and operational efficiency.
  • Help customers and internal teams plan for high-performance compute, storage, networking, and data center capacity.

Build and Evaluate Solutions

  • Develop proof-of-concepts and prototype emerging technologies.
  • Work with technologies from leading infrastructure vendors including Dell, HPE, NVIDIA, Cisco, NetApp, Juniper, and major cloud providers.
  • Leverage automation and Infrastructure-as-Code tools to improve deployment and operational efficiency.

Collaborate Across Teams

  • Partner with facilities, operations, and engineering teams to ensure solutions align with data center space, power, and cooling requirements.
  • Support planning for both traditional enterprise infrastructure and next-generation AI deployments.
  • Share technical guidance with internal stakeholders and customers.

Drive Innovation

  • Participate in research and development initiatives within DRIL.
  • Help evaluate new technologies and identify opportunities to improve performance, sustainability, and operational efficiency.
  • Present findings and recommendations to technical and business audiences.

Share Knowledge

  • Mentor teammates and contribute to a collaborative engineering culture.
  • Create documentation, reference architectures, and best practices that help teams work consistently and efficiently.

What you’ll need

  • Several years of experience designing or implementing enterprise infrastructure solutions.
  • Experience with compute, storage, networking, virtualization, or cloud technologies.
  • Understanding of modern data center infrastructure and enterprise architectures.
  • Strong communication skills and the ability to work effectively with both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
  • A collaborative approach to solving technical challenges.
  • Bachelors or masters degree in related field
  • Experience with AI or high-performance computing infrastructure.
  • Familiarity with GPU-based platforms, Kubernetes, or container technologies.
  • Experience with AWS, Azure, or Google Cloud.
  • Experience using automation tools such as Terraform or Ansible.
  • Knowledge of data center planning, including power, cooling, and rack design.
  • Industry certifications such as AWS, Cisco, NVIDIA, VMware, or PMP.

A bit about us

Digital Realty brings companies and data together by delivering the full spectrum of data center, colocation and interconnection solutions. PlatformDIGITAL®, the company’s global data center platform, provides customers with a secure data meeting place and a proven Pervasive Datacenter Architecture (PDx®) solution methodology for powering innovation and efficiently managing Data Gravity challenges. Digital Realty gives its customers access to the connected data communities that matter to them with a global data center footprint of 300+ facilities in 50+ metros across 25+ countries on six continents.

To learn more about Digital Realty, please visit [digitalrealty.com](http://www.digitalrealty.com/) or follow us on [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/company/digitalrealty) and [Twitter](https://twitter.com/digitalrealty).

What we can offer you

Our rapidly evolving business sector offers the opportunity to be part of a courageous and passionate team who work together to understand and meet the changing needs of our global customers.

Join us and you’ll be part of a supportive and inclusive environment where you can bring your whole self to work. As part of our team, you’ll get to work with people from different business areas, challenge the way we do things and put your ideas into action. We’ll also give you plenty of development opportunities so you can build a rewarding and successful career with us.

Apply today, take charge of your career and grow your talents with us.

Health and Safety

Safety isn't just a priority here at Digital; it's critical to everything we do. Safeguarding lives, protecting assets, and securing data aren't just ideals - they're essential pillars of our commitment to excellence for our people, our partners and our customers. We have a culture of care where every member of Team Digital embraces a relentless pursuit of working safely across Digital Realty. Together we are Safely Powering Progress.

Our Compensation Philosophy

Digital Realty offers its employees a highly competitive compensation package, excellent benefits, and an environment that recognizes and rewards your contributions. Central to our compensation philosophy is rewarding our employees for achieving the values and objectives aligned to the company's overall goals and values.

Your role

This role is ideal for a professional with a blend of strategic architectural expertise and hands-on engineering experience across compute, storage, and networking—plus strong domain knowledge in AI infrastructure, Software Defined Networks and data center space, power, and cooling.

The ideal candidate has 10+ years of experience architecting complex infrastructure solutions, holds a Bachelor’s degree (Master’s preferred) in related field, and thrives in environments that demand innovative thinking, excellent communication, and effective program/project management.

What you’ll do

Solution Selling and Technical Consultation

  • Strong ability to focus ambiguous customer needs into specific, deliverable requirements
  • Able to facilitate workshop style sessions with customers to extract important areas of customers current architecture. Can keenly couple key insights to present highly technical concepts and solutions specifics to audiences of varying technical capabilities in a clear, concise and easily understood manner
  • Professional pre-sales consultation of customer technical requirements to develop viable solutions, resulting in bookings.
  • Quickly and accurately assess current operations, identify opportunities for architectural changes to drive additional business benefit
  • Ability to extract unrealized customer requirements, and service benefits, gaining consensus with data driven positioning.
  • Cost estimation, with a focus of helping customers understand return on investment as well as total cost of ownership advantages of solutions proposed
  • Coach and provide technical leadership to others on network designs, platform sizing, infrastructure system design and the application of new technologies and project management methodologies

Compute, Storage & Networking Implementation

Networking

  • Substantial telecommunications experience required; technical and commercial knowledge of Internet, MPLS and IPVPN topologies and architectures required
  • Proficient in router and switch features and configuration, fault tolerant designs, and QOS mapping
  • Experience with routing and switching protocols; SDN/NFV, performance measurement, tuning and scaling, and reliability and security techniques
  • Experience with Network Peering, Internet Exchanges and CDNs
  • Data center networking technologies and architectures (Leaf-Spine architectures, Data Center Interconnect technologies)
  • Architect and deploy robust infrastructure using hardware/software from vendors such as Dell, HPE, NVIDIA, Cisco, NetApp, and Juniper.
  • Apply deep knowledge of high-performance computing (HPC) and low-latency networking to AI/ML solution design.

Data Center Optimization

  • Collaborate with facilities and operations teams to optimize infrastructure deployments based on available rack space, power draw, thermal dynamics, and airflow efficiency.
  • Contribute to the planning and provisioning of data center resources, ensuring support for both traditional workloads and AI-intensive environments.
  • Evaluate emerging technologies for space, power, and cooling efficiency in next-gen data center deployments.

Enterprise IT

  • Must have a thorough understanding of, and experience with servers, storage, layer 3 networking and enterprise software.  Solid understanding of the entire OSI stack is a must
  • Experience with data center virtualization, software defined data centers and hyper-converged infrastructure solutions
  • Software and Database system development
  • Storage Platform technologies (SAN/NAS) including Hardware and Software (EMC/NetApp/Sun/IBM/HP/VMware/Citrix/Brocade/Juniper)
  • Must have a thorough understanding of the implication of common IT product on system designs: servers, storage, layer 3 networking, and enterprise software.

Innovative Architecture & Infrastructure Design

  • Knowledge of enterprise-grade solutions that integrate hybrid/multi-cloud, AI-ready compute, and intelligent infrastructure platforms.
  • Ensure alignment of technical solutions including Interconnectivity, data center space, power, and cooling capacities, incorporating sustainability and energy-efficiency goals.

Knowledge Sharing

  • Proactively share knowledge and experience across sales and solutions teams to enable continuous learning and best-practice adoption.
  • Develop and maintain reference architectures, design standards, and lab documentation to drive consistency and scalability.

What you’ll need

  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Systems, or a related field required.

  • 10+ years of hands-on experience in network architecture, infrastructure architecture, systems engineering, or solution architecture.

job.title: Senior Manager, Solutions Engineering
job.description:
Job Description

Position Title: Senior Manager, Solutions Engineering

Location: Singapore

Your role

Provides pre-sales technical support to the Sales organisation to ensure that solutions align with customer requirements and provides maximum value to the parties. The Solutions Engineer serves as the “technical face” of Digital Realty and must understand the business, operational and technical requirements of customers and present solutions while considering opportunities for up-sell, geographical cross-sell or unlocking strategic value.

Expected to build strong working relationships with colleagues both within country, within region and across the globe, whilst being the primary technical interface between the various functions involved in supporting our customers.

What you’ll do

  • Support the Enterprise Accounts teams in technical sales and solutions.
  • Direct prospect engagements, including the leading of building and site tours, technical pre-sales calls and proposal generation, pricing and contract negotiations.
  • Understand and document customer technical needs both from a critical infrastructure and fit-out perspective, to then design and present solutions to meet those needs.
  • Where appropriate act as the technical Subject Matter Expert for multi-site deployments, ensuring that the approach to the design, deployment and pricing of solutions is consistent across regions.
  • To be the Subject Matter Experts of your region, involving attaining a deep understanding of the data centres in sub-region including, but not limited to, critical electrical/mechanical infrastructure supporting the whitespace, security features, connectivity services and other site-specific nuances. The Solutions Engineers will take ownership for all technical requirements associated with the opportunities that they support.
  • Liaise with internal stakeholders, including Design Engineering & Construction (DE&C), Service Operations, Customer Success, Asset/Portfolio and Implementation teams to ensure designed solutions meet customer needs whilst adhering to defined standards and production requirements.
  • Work with other Solutions Engineers, Bid Management and Sales to serve as a coordination and review point for technical components of customer RFI/RFPs.
  • Support Design Construction and Engineering (DE&C) Team by providing customer insight into future design workshops.
  • Produce Statements of Works (requirements capture) suitable for third party partners to produce accurate pricing for customer proposals.
  • Participate in forecasting, pipeline and market analysis.
  • Support the Sales teams by engaging in technical requirements capture and defining of technical solutions for a range of customers.
  • Coordinate and perform data centre site tours, providing technical information to the customer before, during and after the tour.
  • Respond effectively, verbally or in writing, to complex inquiries and customer complaints.
  • Facilitate workshop style sessions with customers to extract important aspects of customer requirements.

What you’ll need

  • Bachelor level (e.g. Degree in science, engineering or related discipline or equivalent).
  • Work Experience in the Data Centre sector or telecommunications for at least 5-8 years; Or design consultancy for at least 8-10 years.
  • Prior Management experience is essential.
  • ITIL Expert Certified is desirable but not required.
  • PM Certified is desirable but not required.
  • Experience using CAD, Visio, or other drawing-based software’s (Basic level).
  • Electrical, mechanical, or building services engineering experience.
  • Experience of using tools such as Salesforce, AutoCAD is beneficial.
  • Ability to present complex technical solutions in a simplified manner to articulate solutions and benefits to stakeholders with varying degrees of technical knowledge.
  • Strong ability to focus ambiguous customer needs into specific, deliverable requirements.
  • A strong commitment to delivering excellent customer service to clients and co-workers.
  • Ability to learn and apply technical and business concepts quickly.
  • Work well under pressure and take a proactive approach to unusual occurrences.
  • Ability to clearly communicate solutions and the ability to present to audiences from all levels within an organisation is essential.

Scheduling and Planning:

  • Identify critical path activities and potential schedule risks, proposing mitigation strategies as
  • Coordinate with internal and external stakeholders to align project timelines and ensure timly delivery of required inputs.

projects.

Monitor and support the creation of initial ROM budgets (Gate 1-1) through to presentation of a BTT 1-5 at Gate G1 to the establishment of BTT2-3 and 2-6 to support a Gate G2 approval.

job.title: Design Delivery Manager - Data Centres
job.description:
About Us

Macquarie Data Centres are Australia's most experienced Data Centre Provider and experts in seriously secure, sovereign and compliant data centres.

Our AI and cloud data centres are trusted by the world’s biggest hyperscalers, Global Fortune 500 companies and 42% of the Australian Federal Government. All our campuses are Certified Strategic by the Australian Federal Government and backed by a highly experienced cohort of government cleared engineers.

We are an owned by the ASX listed Macquarie Technology Group.

Step into one of Australia’s most secure, high-performance Data Centres and launch your engineering career supporting mission-critical infrastructure for cloud, defence and enterprise customers.

The Opportunity

This is an opportunity to play a pivotal role in the design and delivery of some of Australia’s most advanced, high-performance data centre infrastructure.

As Design Manager – Engineering Design, you will lead the engineering and technical design of Macquarie Data Centres’ (MDC) data centre projects, delivering innovative, scalable, resilient and compliant solutions for hyperscale and high-density colocation customers.

Reporting to the GM Engineering & Design, you will own the design outcome across the full project lifecycle — from feasibility and due diligence, through concept and detailed design, to issued-for-construction documentation, construction support, commissioning and handover.

You’ll lead and coordinate multidisciplinary internal teams and external engineering consultants, ensuring complex designs are integrated, buildable, commercially sound and delivered to the highest technical standards.

A key focus of the role will be driving Advanced Engineering, Safety in Design, buildability, prefabrication and modularisation, while developing standardised design approaches, optimising long-lead and free-issue equipment, embedding lessons learned and driving sustainability, reliability and commercial value.

This is a role for an experienced design leader who enjoys operating at the intersection of engineering, construction, commercial delivery and customer requirements — and who wants to have a genuine influence on how next-generation data centres are designed and delivered.

The Opportunity

This is an opportunity to play a pivotal role in the design and delivery of some of Australia’s most advanced, high-performance data centre infrastructure.

As Design Manager – Engineering Design, you will lead the engineering and technical design of Macquarie Data Centres’ (MDC) data centre projects, delivering innovative, scalable, resilient and compliant solutions for hyperscale and high-density colocation customers.

Reporting to the GM Engineering & Design, you will own the design outcome across the full project lifecycle — from feasibility and due diligence, through concept and detailed design, to issued-for-construction documentation, construction support, commissioning and handover.

You’ll lead and coordinate multidisciplinary internal teams and external engineering consultants, ensuring complex designs are integrated, buildable, commercially sound and delivered to the highest technical standards.

A key focus of the role will be driving Advanced Engineering, Safety in Design, buildability, prefabrication and modularisation, while developing standardised design approaches, optimising long-lead and free-issue equipment, embedding lessons learned and driving sustainability, reliability and commercial value.

This is a role for an experienced design leader who enjoys operating at the intersection of engineering, construction, commercial delivery and customer requirements — and who wants to have a genuine influence on how next-generation data centres are designed and delivered.

Why Us?

We're Great Place to Work Certified 2023, 2024 and 2025. Australia's #1 [Great Place To Work](https://www.linkedin.com/company/great-place-to-work-us/) in Technology, 2026. For the third year in a row, we have been named a Global Winner of the 2026 Gallup Exceptional Workplace Award! We have the highest Net Promoter Score on the ASX, the [World's best customer experience](https://www.businessthink.unsw.edu.au/articles/macquarie-telecom-tudehope-customer-experience) & [crowned in 2020 at the World Communications Awards](https://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/BU2010/S00476/macquarie-telecom-group-wins-best-customer-experience-in-the-world.htm). You’ll make an impact: Enjoy being part of a driven team with a collaborative culture that values decision-makers and action. We Invest in you: Accelerate your career through our learning and development opportunities - think Gallup strengths-based training, defined career pathways and fantastic internal mobility opportunities across the group.

About You

You are an experienced engineering or design professional with a strong background in data centres, mission-critical infrastructure or similarly complex environments. You bring the technical credibility to lead sophisticated multidisciplinary design teams, combined with the commercial and delivery mindset to turn great engineering into buildable outcomes.

You will have:

  • 8–10+ years’ engineering and design experience, including at least 5 years in data centre or mission-critical environments.
  • A Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, preferably Electrical or Mechanical, or a related technical discipline.
  • Proven experience leading multidisciplinary design across major, complex or fast-tracked projects.
  • Experience managing external engineering consultants and design deliverables from concept through to IFC, construction, as-built and handover.
  • Strong technical understanding across critical data centre services including HV/LV, standby power, UPS, mechanical/cooling, fire, hydraulic, BMS/EPMS, as well as civil, structural and architectural interfaces.
  • Experience working client-side, for a data centre operator, hyperscaler, engineering consultancy or similar environment.
  • Strong understanding of data centre design frameworks including Uptime Institute Tier, TIA-942, NCC/BCA and relevant AS/NZS Standards.
  • Experience with BIM and digital design tools.
  • A strong understanding of buildability, value engineering, cost, program and supply-chain considerations.
  • A genuine commitment to Safety in Design, quality and technical assurance.
  • The ability to influence and challenge consultants and stakeholders while building strong relationships across engineering, construction, procurement, commercial, operations and customer teams.
  • A continuous-improvement mindset, with an interest in innovation, sustainability, energy efficiency, PUE and NABERS for Data Centres.

Why Join Us?

You’ll join a business operating at the forefront of Australia’s data centre industry, where engineering excellence, innovation and speed of delivery are critical.

This is more than a traditional design management role. You’ll have the opportunity to influence design standards, reference designs, prefabrication and modularisation strategies and the way MDC delivers complex mission-critical infrastructure at scale with the newest technology.

You’ll work alongside highly experienced engineering, construction, commercial, procurement and operations professionals and engage directly with specialist equipment manufacturers, authorities, utilities and hyperscale and colocation customers.

If you’re looking for a role where your technical expertise can shape major infrastructure projects from the earliest stages through to operational handover, this is an opportunity to make a significant impact.

If this excites you, apply now, we'd love to hear from you!

job.title: Regional Due Diligence Lead
job.description:
Job Description

Your Role

The Regional Due Diligence Lead for APAC will support all pre-development technical due diligence and site feasibility efforts across the regional portfolio. This role sits within the Design, Engineering & Construction (DE&C) organisation and plays a critical part in evaluating potential data centre developments by assessing technical and commercial viability. The successful candidate will work closely with internal stakeholders, including Acquisitions, Legal, Development, and Design, as well as external consultants, to identify site constraints, risks, costs, and development pathways that inform acquisition decisions and enable successful project delivery.

What you’ll do

  • Own regional due diligence, planning and permitting governance, sequencing and process, continuously improving how we approach our due diligence and entitlement activities.
  • Lead and coordinate all technical due diligence, site feasibility, and development readiness activities for potential site acquisitions globally.
  • Own the technical and commercial assessment of prospective sites within the Preconstruction function, identifying development constraints, risks, opportunities, and costs to support informed acquisition decisions.
  • Assist the Acquisitions team by providing technical input for both existing and new market evaluations.
  • Review seller-provided materials and documentation for accuracy, completeness, development viability, and associated project risks.
  • Develop and execute strategies for entitlements, permitting, and utility connections, working with internal teams and external stakeholders to establish clear development pathways.
  • Engage and support internal teams in managing land use attorneys, civil engineers, environmental, geotechnical, utility, and other specialist consultants to assess project risks, permitting requirements, and development schedules.
  • Collaborate with internal teams (Design, Construction, Masterplanning, Development, Legal, etc.) to consolidate technical inputs and establish comprehensive development schedules for each potential site.
  • Ensure due diligence deliverables align with internal development standards, commercial objectives, and long-term delivery requirements.
  • Structure reports and present findings, risks, recommendations, and development strategies to senior leadership to support investment and acquisition decisions.
  • Develop scalable due diligence processes, standards, and tools to support the continued growth of the global development pipeline.
  • Act as the regional technical due diligence authority, consolidating specialist inputs and providing a clear recommendation on site viability, principal risks, development strategy, cost and schedule assumptions. Final acquisition and investment decisions remain subject to the applicable corporate governance process.

What you’ll need

  • Significant senior-level experience in site development, design, construction, technical due diligence or development management, with a demonstrable track record of leading complex, multi-jurisdictional real estate or infrastructure assessments.
  • Proven experience leading cross-functional due diligence and site feasibility efforts for large-scale real estate or infrastructure projects.
  • Strong understanding of zoning, permitting, entitlements, utility coordination, environmental review processes, and site development regulations.
  • Demonstrated experience developing entitlement, permitting, and utility strategies that enable successful project execution.
  • Excellent organizational and project management skills, with the ability to manage multiple projects and acquisitions concurrently.
  • Experience procuring and managing consultant scopes, schedules, budgets, and technical deliverables.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to present complex technical and commercial findings clearly to executive stakeholders.
  • Ability to work independently while collaborating effectively across multidisciplinary global teams.
  • Bachelor’s degree in engineering, architecture, construction management, real estate development or a related discipline, or equivalent relevant professional experience. A relevant postgraduate qualification is desirable.
  • Multi-jurisdictional planning and permitting environments and tracking of utility capacity, connection strategy and programme risks associated with permitting.
  • Environmental, ground, flood, transport and infrastructure constraints.
  • Provide risk-based recommendations for investment governance and consultant procurement and management across countries.
  • Ability to travel across APAC and to work across cultures, time zones and regulatory regimes.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with data centre development or hyperscale infrastructure is highly desirable.
  • Familiarity with land acquisition, entitlement, and permitting frameworks across multiple international jurisdictions.
  • Relevant professional membership, chartership or certification, such as CEng, PEP, Eur Ing, RICS, CIOB, RIBA, PMI/PMP or an equivalent national or international qualification, is desirable.

job.title: Senior Manager, Commercial
job.description:
Join DayOne – Shaping the Future of Data Infrastructure

DayOne is a global leader in the development and operation of high-performance data centers. As one of the fastest-growing companies in the industry, we’ve built a robust presence across Asia and Europe — and we’re just getting started.

As we expand into new international markets, we’re looking for talented, driven individuals to join us on this exciting journey. This is more than a job — it’s an opportunity to be a key contributor to our dynamic team and help shape the future of global data infrastructure.

If you're passionate about innovation, technology, and growth, we invite you to be part of DayOne’s next chapter.

About the role

The purpose of this role is to drive and manage commercial aspects of customer prospects across DayOne’s portfolio of data centres globally. You will be responsible for managing the profitability of DayOne’s customers, including reviewing, negotiating and overseeing contracts, pursuing new business opportunities and supporting sales and marketing strategies.

You must have a good knowledge of the ICT and data centre market and possess strong commercial acumen. This role will be based in Singapore.

Key Responsibilities

  • Lead strategic pricing for bids/RFPs and non-standard or complex products/solutions
  • Conduct commercial risk assessment for customer contracts and other strategic initiatives / investment. Work with all business units (eg legal) to review non-standard contracts or non-standard terms
  • Drive the review/approval process with Deal Committee for proposals that are non-standard/complex/capex-intensive
  • Provide support to Sales on commercial proposals (pricing and costing). Perform win-loss analysis.
  • Co-drive regular review of costing / pricing in the various markets with Sales and Product.
  • Co-drive the review the renewal / churn of service agreements / leases with Sales
  • Prepare Sales forecast and pipeline analysis
  • Proactively present suggestions for process/business improvements and assume accountability for implementation of relevant initiatives.
  • Drives the digitizing of commercial and quotation processes to improve efficiency

Qualifications and experience required

  • Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Business, Economics, Engineering, IT, or a related field.
  • Minimum 6 years of relevant experience in business analysis, preferably in a data centre, IT infrastructure, telecommunications, or technology environment.
  • Detail-oriented, self-motivated, and capable of managing multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills
  • Strong commercial acumen
  • Financial knowledge to build business cases and financial models
  • Appreciation of technical knowledge of data centres, telecommunications and other technologies relevant to data centres
  • Strong stakeholder management and interpersonal skills
  • Proficient in Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, PowerPoint etc)

DayOne is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

If you're ready to grow with one of the fastest-moving companies in the data center industry, apply now and be part of our global journey.

About the Role

We are seeking a dynamic leader who can build exceptional teams, lead mission-critical operations, and drive business performance across a growing portfolio of data centers.

As Director, Data Center Operations, you will be responsible for the leadership, performance, and strategic direction of multiple data center operations functions. You will oversee operational excellence, customer experience, financial performance, talent development, critical infrastructure reliability, and long-term site strategy while partnering closely with senior business leaders.

Success in this role requires a unique combination of people leadership, business acumen, and technical expertise.

What You'll Do

Lead and Develop High-Performing Teams

  • Lead, coach, recruit, and develop managers and operational teams across multiple sites.
  • Build a strong leadership pipeline through mentoring, succession planning, and capability development.
  • Foster a culture of accountability, inclusion, collaboration, safety, and continuous improvement.
  • Drive workforce planning strategies that support business growth and operational readiness.

Drive Business Performance

  • Own operational performance across a portfolio of mission-critical facilities.
  • Lead budgeting, forecasting, capital planning, and financial management activities.
  • Evaluate investment decisions and operational trade-offs by balancing customer experience, risk, reliability, and business outcomes.
  • Partner with commercial, operational, and executive stakeholders to support business growth, strategic initiatives, and customer success.

  • Lead major incident response, risk management, root cause investigations, and corrective action programs.

Qualifications

job.title: Data Center Critical Facilities V - Singapore
job.description:
Job Summary

The Senior Critical Facilities Engineer (Electrical) is a senior technical specialist responsible for ensuring the reliability, availability, and safe operation of mission-critical power infrastructure within the data center environment. This role provides technical leadership for electrical operations, maintenance, troubleshooting, and incident response activities while supporting the continuous delivery of highly resilient services to customers.

Working with a high degree of independence, the engineer leads complex electrical maintenance activities, supports critical switching operations, identifies operational risks, and drives continuous improvement initiatives that enhance infrastructure reliability, safety, and efficiency.

Responsibilities

Facility / Infrastructure Maintenance

  • Operate, maintain, and support mission-critical electrical infrastructure, including UPS systems, generators, switchgear, transformers, PDUs, breakers, and associated distribution systems
  • Perform advanced preventive and corrective maintenance activities to ensure the reliability and availability of critical power systems
  • Lead electrical troubleshooting efforts and resolve complex infrastructure issues, minimizing operational risk and customer impact
  • Monitor the Building Management System (BMS) and Electrical Power Monitoring Systems (EPMS), responding to alarms and identifying potential risks before service impacts occur
  • Lead and coordinate critical electrical operations, including maintenance windows, switching procedures, energization activities, and infrastructure recovery efforts
  • Conduct site inspections and assess the health and performance of electrical infrastructure, recommending corrective actions and reliability improvements
  • Support electrical capacity planning and load management activities to ensure infrastructure readiness for future growth
  • Identify opportunities to improve system reliability, operational efficiency, and energy performance

Site Administration

  • Prepare, review, and authorize technical documentation including Maintenance Operation Protocols (MOPs), Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), Emergency Operating Procedures (EOPs), and switching plans
  • Ensure maintenance activities are executed safely and in accordance with operational, regulatory, and company requirements
  • Maintain accurate infrastructure records, maintenance history, and operational documentation

Incident Management

  • Serve as a technical lead during electrical incidents, infrastructure failures, and power-related events
  • Provide guidance to on-site teams during incident response and restoration activities
  • Conduct root cause analysis (RCA) investigations and develop corrective and preventive action plans
  • Lead post-incident reviews and recommend improvements to operational processes and infrastructure resilience

Vendor Management

  • Manage and coordinate electrical service providers, contractors, and vendors performing maintenance and project activities
  • Review vendor work plans, technical proposals, and maintenance recommendations
  • Ensure work is performed in accordance with safety requirements, industry standards, and data center operational procedures

Work Orders & Capacity Management

  • Lead resolution of complex work orders and infrastructure-related requests
  • Support electrical capacity planning, power utilization analysis, and infrastructure growth initiatives
  • Provide technical reviews of customer power requirements and infrastructure impacts
  • Support commissioning, testing, and integration of new electrical systems

Collaboration

  • Act as a technical mentor to engineers and technicians, sharing expertise and supporting team development
  • Partner with Critical Facilities, Customer Operations, Security, Design & Construction, and vendor teams to deliver operational excellence
  • Identify underlying infrastructure issues and recommend long-term reliability improvements
  • Leverage internal and external technical resources to resolve complex electrical challenges

Additional Projects

  • Lead electrical infrastructure projects, including upgrades, capacity expansion, modernization, and reliability improvement initiatives
  • Support lifecycle management and replacement strategies for critical electrical assets
  • Participate in commissioning, integrated systems testing, and acceptance activities for new infrastructure deployments
  • Recommend and champion initiatives that improve uptime, reliability, safety, and operational efficiency

Qualifications

Education & Experience

  • Diploma or Degree in Electrical Engineering, Power Engineering, or a related discipline preferred
  • Minimum 5 years of experience operating and maintaining critical electrical infrastructure in data centers, utilities, industrial facilities, telecommunications, or other mission-critical environments

Preferred Skills & Experience

  • Strong experience with mission-critical power systems, including: UPS systems Diesel generators Switchgear and breakers Transformers Low- and medium-voltage distribution systems Power monitoring systems
  • Experience performing electrical switching activities, maintenance planning, and incident response
  • Ability to troubleshoot complex electrical faults and identify root causes
  • Experience leading maintenance vendors and coordinating infrastructure projects
  • Strong understanding of electrical safety practices, operational risk management, and permit-to-work processes

job.title: Data Center Safety Manager (36-Month Contract)
job.description:
About the Role

The Safety Manager is to lead and implement health, safety, and environmental programs across mission-critical data center operations and projects. This role is responsible for driving a strong safety culture, ensuring regulatory compliance, managing operational and construction-related risks, and supporting safe, reliable data center environments.

What You'll Do

  • Lead HSE programs and initiatives across data center operations, maintenance, and construction activities.
  • Promote a proactive safety culture and ensure compliance with company, client, and regulatory requirements.
  • Monitor and manage safety risks associated with critical facilities, including electrical systems, mechanical infrastructure, contractor activities, and commissioning works.
  • Conduct risk assessments, audits, inspections, and incident investigations to identify and mitigate potential hazards.
  • Track HSE performance metrics and drive continuous improvement initiatives.
  • Partner with operations, engineering, project, and vendor teams to ensure safe work practices and permit-to-work compliance.
  • Develop and deliver HSE training, toolbox talks, and emergency preparedness programs.
  • Support client reporting and ensure alignment with global EHS standards and best practices.

What You'll Need

  • Bachelor's Degree in Occupational Safety, Environmental Science, Engineering, or a related discipline.
  • 5+ years of HSE experience within data centers, mission-critical facilities, construction, engineering, or industrial environments.
  • Strong knowledge of regulatory compliance, risk assessment, incident investigation, and contractor safety management.
  • Experience managing high-risk activities such as electrical work, confined space entry, working at heights, lifting operations, and commissioning activities.
  • Excellent stakeholder management, communication, and leadership skills.

job.title: EHS Director
job.description:
Join DayOne – Shaping the Future of Data Infrastructure

DayOne is a global leader in the development and operation of high-performance data centers. As one of the fastest-growing companies in the industry, we’ve built a robust presence across Asia and Europe — and we’re just getting started.

As we expand into new international markets, we’re looking for talented, driven individuals to join us on this exciting journey. This is more than a job — it’s an opportunity to be a key contributor to our dynamic team and help shape the future of global data infrastructure.

If you're passionate about innovation, technology, and growth, we invite you to be part of DayOne’s next chapter.

Position Summary

The Director, EHS Center of Excellence (CoE), is responsible for establishing, governing, and continuously improving DayOne's global Environmental, Health & Safety management framework across all operational and construction business units. This role serves as the global authority for EHS standards, management systems, certification programs, contractor governance, audit assurance, and regulatory best practices.

The Director will lead the development and deployment of standardized EHS programs, minimum requirements, performance assurance systems, contractor qualification processes, and certification initiatives to ensure consistent implementation across all regions. The role will work closely with regional EHS teams, project delivery teams, operations teams, procurement, and business leaders to drive EHS excellence, regulatory compliance, operational discipline, and continuous improvement.

Key Responsibilities

1. Global EHS Standards & Governance

  • Develop, maintain, and continuously enhance DayOne Global EHS Management System (EHSMS).
  • Establish global EHS policies, standards, procedures, guidelines, and minimum requirements applicable across all regions and business units.
  • Define governance frameworks to ensure consistent implementation of EHS expectations throughout the organization.
  • Lead periodic reviews and revisions of corporate EHS standards to align with evolving regulations, industry best practices, customer requirements, and business needs.
  • Develop standardized EHS tools, templates, reporting requirements, and performance measurement systems.

2. Management Systems & Certification

  • Lead the implementation, maintenance, and continual improvement of ISO 14001, ISO 45001, and other relevant certification programs.
  • Serve as corporate owner for all EHS certifications and related management systems.
  • Coordinate external certification audits, surveillance audits, and recertification activities.
  • Conduct management reviews and oversee closure of audit findings and corrective actions.
  • Benchmark DayOne EHS management systems against industry best practices and leading data center operators.
  • Support future certification initiatives required by customers, investors, or regulatory authorities.

3. General Contractor (GC) Governance & Assurance

  • Develop and maintain the global General Contractor EHS Qualification and Pre-Qualification Program.
  • Establish minimum EHS and ESG requirements for contractor selection and engagement.
  • Lead contractor onboarding programs to ensure alignment with DayOne EHS expectations.
  • Develop contractor performance evaluation methodologies and governance frameworks.
  • Oversee contractor EHS performance monitoring, trend analysis, and corrective action management.
  • Partner with Procurement, Legal, and Project Delivery teams to strengthen contractor risk management practices.

4. Global Audit & Assurance Program

  • Develop and implement a risk-based Global EHS Audit and Surveillance Program.
  • Establish audit protocols, methodologies, checklists, and scoring systems.
  • Lead corporate audits of construction projects, operational data centers, and contractor activities.
  • Monitor closure of audit findings, observations, and corrective actions.
  • Analyze audit trends and identify systemic improvement opportunities.
  • Provide independent assurance to senior leadership regarding EHS performance and compliance maturity.

5. EHS Capability Development

  • Establish global EHS competency frameworks for employees, contractors, and leadership teams.
  • Develop EHS training, awareness, and certification programs.
  • Create onboarding requirements for newly appointed EHS personnel and key operational stakeholders.
  • Lead knowledge-sharing initiatives and global EHS communities of practice.
  • Promote a culture of learning, accountability, and operational excellence.

6. Incident Learning & Continuous Improvement

  • Establish corporate incident reporting, investigation, and lessons-learned frameworks.
  • Lead reviews of significant incidents, high-potential events, and regulatory matters.
  • Oversee root cause analysis methodologies and corrective action effectiveness reviews.
  • Publish global alerts, lessons learned, and best practice guidance.
  • Identify recurring trends and drive preventive programs across the organization.

7. Performance Management & Reporting

  • Develop enterprise EHS KPIs, leading indicators, lagging indicators, and performance dashboards.
  • Establish benchmarking metrics across projects, regions, and business units.
  • Analyze organizational performance trends and identify improvement opportunities.
  • Prepare periodic reports and presentations for executive leadership, EHS Committees, customers, and Board-level stakeholders.
  • Support ESG and sustainability reporting related to EHS performance.

8. Regulatory & Industry Engagement

  • Monitor emerging EHS regulations and industry developments globally.
  • Develop compliance strategies to address evolving regulatory requirements.
  • Engage with external industry associations, certification bodies, regulators, customers, and consultants.
  • Represent DayOne in EHS industry forums, working groups, and customer assurance engagements.

Leadership Responsibilities

  • Lead and develop the Global EHS Center of Excellence team.
  • Provide technical guidance and strategic support to Regional EHS Managers and site teams.
  • Foster collaboration across EHS, Operations, Construction, Procurement, HR, Legal, and Corporate Functions.
  • Drive a culture of EHS excellence, accountability, innovation, and continuous improvement.

Qualifications

Education

  • Bachelor's Degree in Occupational Health & Safety, Environmental Science, Engineering, or a related discipline.
  • Master's Degree preferred.

Professional Certifications

  • Certified Safety Professional (CSP), NEBOSH Diploma, CRSP, WSHO, or equivalent.
  • ISO 14001 and/or ISO 45001 Lead Auditor certification preferred.

Experience

  • Minimum 15 years of progressive EHS experience.
  • Minimum 8 years in a senior leadership or corporate governance role.
  • Experience managing EHS programs across multiple countries and regions.
  • Demonstrated experience implementing ISO management systems and certification programs.
  • Extensive experience developing contractor governance, qualification, and audit programs.
  • Experience supporting large-scale construction and critical infrastructure/data center operations is highly desirable.

Competencies

  • Strategic leadership and business partnership.
  • Strong audit and management system expertise.
  • Exceptional stakeholder management and influence skills.
  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, and risk management capabilities.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
  • Ability to work effectively across diverse cultures and geographies.

DayOne is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

If you're ready to grow with one of the fastest-moving companies in the data center industry, apply now and be part of our global journey.

  • Qualified to Diploma/Degree Level in Mechanical Engineering with a minimum of 3 years direct industry experience or a minimum of 8 years' experience at Mechanical Technician level in a critical environment combined with supervisory experience. Preference is given to data centre, hospital, pharmaceutical production.
  • An excellent understanding and experience of the mechanical and control systems used in a data centre environment, including: Fuel Systems, Building Management Systems and Controls, Chilled water cooling plant, Air handling units, Variable Frequency Drives (VSDs), Fire Alarm systems, and Fire Suppression systems (pre-action sprinklers).
  • Experience of complex automatic control equipment, including relay logic, programmable logic controllers (PLC's), building management systems, and their integration with the data centre infrastructure.
  • Extensive experience of large scale chilled water plant including chillers, chilled water distribution and storage systems, cooling towers, and chemical dosing systems
  • Experience of working within a Project Environment and dealing with design and construction engineering professionals
  • Strong oral and written communication skills, with the ability to communicate intelligently and effectively with the client and with contractors who perform maintenance or upgrade work on the data centre systems.
  • Computer literate with the ability to compile and submit monthly and annual reports, and to monitor and trend operational characteristics (load, capacity, environmental conditions etc).
  • Strong and committed team player with excellent communication and coaching skills. Previous experience of supervising highly qualified Technicians and reporting to peers and senior managers.
  • Willingness to work outside of normal hours to resolve technical issues in a 24/7 industry
  • The ability to learn quickly and to gain maximum benefit from extensive training and development programmes aimed at ensuring that any identified knowledge or experience deficiencies are addressed in the short term.

job.title: Associate Director, Security Programs & Assurance
job.description:
Want to be a part of Asia Pacific & Middle East's (APME) largest, most innovative, and rapidly growing data centre company?

AirTrunk is a technology company with a powerful purpose - to scale and sustain the relentless growth of the region’s digital future. We do this by continuously redefining and delivering hyperscale data centres that meet the needs of our customers - the world’s most transformational companies. And we’re doing so sustainably, for today and tomorrow.

Having opened Australia’s first and largest hyperscale data centres in 2017, we set our eyes on rapid expansion and now operate a platform of hyperscale data centres across the APME region. With backing from our investors, including Blackstone, this is just the beginning…

Come join the A-Team at AirTrunk, where the cloud meets the ground.

Your Impact

As the Associate Director, Security Programs & Assurance based in our HQ in Melbourne, you will report to the Director, Security and work closely with various teams and leadership across the Asia Pacific region and beyond, making your mark in a number of ways:

  • Lead the governance, quality assurance, and continuous improvement of all AirTrunk data centre physical security designs across the project lifecycle.
  • Be the primary authority for data centre security design assurance, providing oversight and challenge to internal teams, consultants, contractors, and technology vendors to ensure data centre security designs consistently meet AirTrunk standards, customer requirements, regulatory obligations, and industry best practices.
  • Establish and maintain a robust security design review framework, ensuring that all physical security systems, components, and operational security requirements are effectively embedded into new builds, expansions, and major upgrade projects.

What You'll Do

Security Design Quality Assurance

  • Develop, implement, and maintain security design governance frameworks, standards, and review processes.
  • Conduct formal design reviews and assurance activities at key project milestones, including, Master Planning, Concept Design, Schematic Design, Detailed Design, Construction Documentation, Commissioning and Handover.
  • Ensure all security designs align with AirTrunk security standards, operational requirements, customer commitments, and applicable regulations.
  • Identify design deficiencies, risks, or gaps and drive remediation actions with stakeholders.
  • Review and approve proposed changes to security designs throughout project delivery and assess the operational, commercial and security impacts of these changes.
  • Provide formal security design acceptance recommendations and approval support.

Security-by-Design Leadership

  • Act as the accountable subject matter expert and leader for all physical security data centre security designs and threat vulnerability risk assessments.
  • Evaluate emerging technologies and recommend design enhancements that improve security effectiveness, resilience, and operational efficiency.
  • Ensure security considerations are incorporated into campus master planning and future growth strategies.
  • Coach and mentor team members and build organisational capability in security design assurance.

Technical Security Oversight

  • Provide technical assurance leadership to a group of regional Security Program Managers across all physical security domains, including, Access Control Systems, Video Surveillance Systems (CCTV), Perimeter Detection Systems, Intrusion Detection Systems, Security Operations Centre integrations, Security Communications Systems, Visitor Management Systems, Identity Management integrations, Control Room Design, Critical Infrastructure Protection requirements.
  • Define lifecycle replacement strategies for security technologies to ensure resilience, supportability and alignment with business requirements.
  • Evaluate product obsolescence and develop upgrade strategies.
  • Document security maintenance specifications and support regional security integrator tenders as a technical SME lead.

Cyber security integration for physical security platforms.

  • Ensure security systems support scalability, cyber resilience and operational supportability and comply with AirTrunk cyber security requirements.
  • Collaborate with Cyber Security teams to manage vulnerabilities, hardening standards and secure system configurations.

Program and Stakeholder Management

  • Partner with Development, Design, Construction, ICT, Operations, Risk, and Customer Solutions teams to ensure consistent application of security standards.
  • Manage global relationships with security consultants, architects, engineers, integrators, and technology vendors..
  • Prepare reports, recommendations and strategic updates for Executive Leadership on security design risks, emerging threats and portfolio performance.
  • Influence decision-making across multiple stakeholders and project teams throughout the project lifecycle.

Standards and Compliance

  • Maintain AirTrunk security standards, specifications, and technical guidelines.
  • Monitor industry trends, emerging threats, and best practices to continuously improve design standards.
  • Ensure compliance with customer security requirements, internal governance frameworks, applicable legislation and regulations, industry standards and security frameworks.
  • Support internal and external audits as required, including Australian Government security audits.

Continuous Improvement

  • Establish metrics and performance indicators for security design quality.
  • Conduct post-project reviews and lessons-learned activities.
  • Drive standardisation and repeatability across AirTrunk's global portfolio.
  • Lead initiatives to improve security design maturity, efficiency, and resilience

Operational readiness and transition to business-as-usual

  • Assist operational readiness reviews for security systems prior to handover.
  • Assist to ensure operational documentation, training, maintenance strategies and support models are established before project completion.

Customer Engagement

  • Translate customer security needs into actionable design requirements for colocation, build to suit and fit to suit customer security standards.
  • Participate in customer negotiations and presentations, representing AirTrunk Security on matters including physical security and design expectations.
  • Support the development of Statements of Qualifications (SOQs), RFP responses, and other tender submissions, ensuring the security narrative is clear, accurate, and satisfactory for AirTrunks customers.
  • Assist with customer contract reviews to ensure security clauses meet AirTrunk standards and regional compliance requirements.

What You'll Bring

  • 10+years in physical security, security engineering, critical infrastructure, or data centre environments.
  • Tertiary and/or industry qualifications in security or a related field.
  • Demonstrated experience reviewing and approving complex physical security designs.
  • In-depth knowledge of security risk management strategies and processes, including security threat vulnerability risk assessment.
  • Strong knowledge of enterprise physical security systems and technologies.
  • Experience managing external design consultants and system integrators.
  • Strong understanding of project delivery and design management methodologies.
  • Competent written, verbal and data presentation skills in English.
  • Well-developed communication, collaboration, influence and conflict resolution skills.
  • Ability to thrive in a fast-paced changing environment and work effectively in a team environment.
  • Strong forward-planning and portfolio governance capability.
  • Ability to balance operational, commercial, customer, and security considerations.
  • Experience influencing security teams, management, and contractors.
  • Ability to work effectively across diverse functions and geographies.

job.title: Engineer, Technical Officer, Technician, Facility Management
job.description:
JOB DESCRIPTION

Customer Service

  • Maintain a positive and professional working relationship with internal and external clients.
  • Respond to customer service requests in a timely manner.
  • Respond to emergency calls (during shift work).

Maintain Data Center Systems

  • Assist the Operation Lead in the daily management of the DC Operations and Periodic Preventive Maintenance Management ensuring 100% uptime of the Dc critical M&E systems.
  • Conduct daily walkthrough of DC to record and report any faults or defects detected and take down record of M&E equipment.
  • Ensure that the FOC is monitored and manned at all times and that EPMS, BMS, and Fire System alarms are responded to in a timely manner; contain/isolate the fault identified and provide impromptu escalations/updates base on escalation plan laid.
  • Conduct daily routine checklist to ensure no environmental abnormalities and all critical M&E related systems are in good working condition.
  • Ensure all subcontractors are inducted and permitted to work within the Critical Environment domain. Review subcontractor method statements, risk assessments, and MSDS to ensure compliance with site health & safety and operating procedures.
  • Maintain log and records of instrument readings, equipment and consumable stock level.
  • Report all unlocked doors and racks to the security control.
  • Briefing and handover to Shift Duty Technician on all outstanding issues and Standing Instructions from the Operation Lead / Assistant Manager / Manager.
  • Incidents and field service reporting and filing.
  • Adherence to all quality, health & safety, and environmental policies within the CE domain.
  • Comply to site required policies, guidelines and practices.

JOB REQUIREMENTS

Qualified candidates will possess the following:

  • ITE/Nitec/Diploma in Electrical or Mechanical Engineering, Facilities Management, or equivalent field of study required.
  • An excellent understanding and experience of the electrical and mechanical systems used in a data center environment, including: Feeders, Transformers, Generators, Fuel Systems, Switchgear, UPS systems, Battery banks, ATS/STS units, PDU/PMM units, Chillers, Air handling units, Chilled water plant, CRAC units, Fire Alarm systems, and Fire Suppression systems.
  • Experience of complex automatic control equipment, including relay logic, programmable logic controllers (PLC's), building management systems, and their integration with the data center infrastructure.
  • Advanced knowledge of Microsoft Office Suite - Word, Excel, Outlook and Visio required; working knowledge of SharePoint preferred.
  • Proficiency in both written and spoken English.
  • 3 to 5 or more years of experience in a data center or other Critical Environment required (preference is given to data center, hospital, pharmaceutical production or power plant experience).
  • Working knowledge of mechanical, electrical, life safety monitoring and control systems typically used in critical environments.
  • Proficient knowledge of HVAC and/or Electrical Systems. Team Lead shall be proficient in both Electrical and Mechanical.
  • Able to work rotating shifts and on weekends/public holidays.

job.title: Associate, Investment
job.description:
JOB DESCRIPTION

This is a key role that focuses on supporting infrastructure investments in Keppel, managing the end-to-end investment process from underwriting potential investment opportunities, transactions management, deal conclusion with the various stakeholders, as well as, post-deal management. The key objective of this role will be to contribute to the execution and delivery of maximizing the risk-adjusted returns for the investments.

Key Responsibilities

  • Support the senior team in identifying and evaluating potential investment opportunities, underwriting, structuring and executing transactions in Asia Pacific and other regions
  • Conduct, review and maintain detailed financial modelling to assess or support prospective investments; Present financial analysis to key stakeholders
  • Conduct and coordinate various due diligence work streams including but not limited to legal, financial, tax, commercial, technical and ESG due diligence for potential investments, working with internal functional teams and external advisers/ consultants
  • Work with internal functional teams and external advisors to plan, negotiate and structure deal documentation, contracts and financing
  • Prepare investment papers, presentations and other materials as required
  • Project manage investment and divestment processes including participation in both auction and bilateral/ off-market transactions
  • Support the planning and implementation of strategies around asset management including working alongside the investee companies on post-closing initiatives, i.e., integration plan, overseeing company’s performance, executing the business plan and investment exits.
  • Responsible for periodic reporting, i.e., quarterly and annual investor meeting, and assist in developing marketing or communication materials for internal and external use

JOB REQUIREMENTS

Requirements

  • 2-4 years of relevant investment experience ideally in fund management or corporate finance/ M&A/ valuation in investment banks or corporate principal investment teams or accounting firms, focused on the infrastructure sector; Candidate with less years of experience but with superior relevant experience and skill sets would also be considered
  • Strong academic qualifications
  • Proficient with market and industry research in infrastructure
  • Proactively manage and respond to daily tasks, detailed-oriented, willing and able to get hands dirty to meet targets with limited supervision
  • Ability to multi-task, prioritize and work in a fast pace dynamic environment with high degree of flexibility and adaptability
  • Independent and critical thinker with exceptional analytical ability; strong financial modelling skills
  • The ability to make effective investment and asset management decisions
  • Excellent stakeholder management skills and ability to build relationships and interact well with different functions and levels
  • Excellent written and oral communication and presentation and interpersonal skills. Strong ability to communicate via Power Point, excel and orally
  • Possess strong work ethic, accountability and a passion for excellence
  • Willing to travel frequently, if required, to various key markets

job.title: Associate, Portfolio Management
job.description:
JOB DESCRIPTION

Job Purpose

The Associate, Portfolio Management will support the CEO and senior portfolio management team in monitoring, analysing and managing Keppel Infrastructure Trust (KIT)’s portfolio. The role focuses on data-driven analysis, portfolio monitoring, financial modelling and preparation of materials to support investment decisions, portfolio optimisation and capital allocation, with the objective of delivering sustainable, risk‑adjusted returns.

Key Responsibilities

Portfolio Monitoring & Analysis

  • Support ongoing portfolio monitoring by gathering operational and financial data from portfolio companies.
  • Conduct quantitative and qualitative analysis on portfolio performance, risks, value drivers and returns.
  • Assist in identifying performance gaps, emerging risks and improvement opportunities across assets.

Portfolio Strategy & Capital Allocation

  • Support evaluation of portfolio construction and capital allocation considerations based on long‑term market outlook, asset performance and strategic priorities.
  • Contribute analysis to the refinement of investment and asset management strategies in line with KIT’s long‑term objectives.

Investment & Asset Management Support

  • Assist in preparing analysis and materials for strategy discussions with KIT management and portfolio companies.
  • Support shareholder decision-making processes, including preparation of papers and tracking of resolutions.
  • Support budget reviews and cash flow analysis of portfolio companies.

Transactions & Capital Management

  • Support acquisitions and divestments through financial modelling, due diligence analysis and coordination with internal and external stakeholders.
  • Assist in capital raising activities, including preparation of presentation materials, data analysis and coordination with finance and legal teams.

Reporting & Investor Support

  • Work with finance and asset management teams to prepare periodic portfolio and management reporting.
  • Support investor relations activities, including preparation of materials for unitholder updates and investor communications.

JOB REQUIREMENTS

Requirements

  • Degree in Business, Finance, Economics or related disciplines.
  • 2–4 years of relevant experience in infrastructure, private equity investment, investment banking, corporate finance or consultancy.
  • Strong analytical and financial modelling skills with solid commercial acumen.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills;
  • Ability to manage multiple workstreams in a fast‑paced, collaborative environment.

job.title: Shift Operations Technician
job.description:
JOB DESCRIPTION

  • Support Operations Engineer to monitor plant status via the Central Control Room (CCR), tracking variables for boilers, turbo-generators, and flue gas treatment auxiliaries.
  • Assist in safe equipment isolation and normalization using P&ID drawings.
  • Support operations involving weighbridges, water/wastewater treatment, reception halls, and bunker management.
  • Assist to handle and resolve technical issues related to daily generation and processing units.
  • Support to enforce the PTW system, risk assessments, and Lockout-Tagout system.
  • Participate actively in plant safety initiatives, toolbox talks, and workplace health standards.
  • Work alongside maintenance teams during boiler and turbo-generator overhauls.
  • Contribute to plant improvement, efficiency, and ad-hoc engineering tasks assigned by supervisors.
  • Carry out routine checks and testing of plant equipment and propose job cards in a proper manner
  • Monitor plant parameters and make adjustments/troubleshoot via DCS or in the site to ensure parameters are within limits, including temperature, pressure, flue gas emissions, etc
  • Manage boiler water condition and level, including monitoring and controlling water consumption
  • Perform the necessary equipment switch-over, like feed water pumps, flue gas treatment compartment, chemical dosing silo, etc.
  • Optimize refuse incineration throughput based on operating conditions
  • Ensure chemicals and consumables optimization
  • Record and document changes in work procedures accurately and precisely according to plant ISO standards and quality management procedures
  • Update plant status – informing equipment failure or situation in time to immediate superior
  • Ensure that incidents (if any) are well-handled and properly documented with minimum disruption to operations
  • Enforcement of Permit-to-Work (PTW) System with good Risk Assessment System in line with identified Work Inventory. Administer PTW system and LOTO well
  • Assist in isolation and normalization of equipment safely based on plant P&ID drawings
  • Assist the Operations Engineer in management of activities for Operations with regard to Central Control Room (CCR), Weighbridge, Water and Wastewater Treatment Plant, Overhaul, reception hall, bunker management and other general plant matters
  • Handle and resolve all technical issues related to operations of boilers, turbo-generators, Flue gas treatment and its auxiliaries
  • Ensure smooth and efficient operation of turbo-generators and associated common equipment
  • Work with Maintenance team on carrying out Boiler and Turbo-Generators overhaul and any ad hoc work activities
  • Have a safety mindset and participate actively in safety initiatives and events
  • Contribute to improvement and optimization projects
  • Any other ad-hoc duties assigned by supervisor / plant management

JOB REQUIREMENTS

  • At least a Higher NITEC in Mechanical, Chemical, Electrical Engineering or equivalent
  • Working knowledge of the principles and mechanics of plant equipment and DCS functions is essential
  • At least a Class 2 Boiler Attendant Certificate is preferred but not mandatory
  • Preferably have attended training relating to HAZMAT/First Aid/Incident Management/Work-at-Height/Confined Space. Trainings will be planned for those who have not been trained
  • Strong safety mindset and can-do attitude
  • Meticulous with good interpersonal and communication skills
  • Good team-player with high initiative
  • An interest in process or Waste-to-Energy (WTE) Plant operations. Must be able to get accustomed to WTE environment
  • Committed to 12-hour shift work and willing to provide support on off/rest day when required
  • This is a 2 years contract position.

About Us

CDC Data Centres is Australia’s leading operator of sovereign, secure, world-class data centre facilities. Headquartered in Canberra with multiple facilities across ACT, NSW, VIC and New Zealand, CDC’s diversified operations provide secure data centre configurations that support co-location, containerised and hyperscale compute environments with all campuses interconnected with high-speed carrier grade networks.

At CDC we are passionate about creating an inclusive workplace that promotes and values diversity.
