Together, we configure the landscape to meet the security, reliability, connectivity and sustainability needs for today and tomorrow.

About the Role

At CDC, our Critical Environment Technicians work hands-on in live data centres, supporting the day-to-day operation of mission critical infrastructure. This is a site-based role focused on planned works, maintenance, site logistics, and overall reliability during business hours.

You’ll play a key role in delivering technical facilities management — coordinating maintenance, managing site operations, and responding to incidents to keep our environments safe, secure, and always on.

If you’ve worked in electrical, HVAC, or industrial environments, much of this will feel familiar. The difference is the scale, the environment, and the opportunity to step into a stable, high-growth industry.

You’ll be part of CDC’s Operations team — on the ground every day, working closely together to deliver a strong customer experience and keep our facilities running at their best.

What you’ll be doing day‑to‑day:

  • Monitoring and responding to alarms and alerts across power, cooling, and fire systems
  • Performing physical inspections to ensure equipment and infrastructure are operating within defined parameters
  • Responding to faults and incidents, prioritising actions, and determining when escalation or contractor support is required
  • Carrying out operational switching and control activities to prevent unplanned outages
  • Supporting planned maintenance and monitoring contractors on site, ensuring strict adherence to safety procedures and approved methods of operation
  • Documenting incidents, maintenance activities, and observations to support continuous improvement

Benefits, Training and Offerings:

Our training program provides tailored content through our CDC Academy, specifically designed for individuals starting out in this role. You'll learn hands-on by shadowing and working alongside our experienced Service Technicians, gaining essential knowledge to develop your skillset.

  • CDC Social Events - CDC’s offers staff and their family’s inclusive events that nurtures relationships, connection and friendships across the business. CDC hosts BBQs, family picnics and community events, bringing together CDC staff in different settings.

About You

You have experience working in environments where reliability, safety, and procedure matter - whether that’s through an electrical, HVAC, mechanical, or broader critical infrastructure background.

You might be a qualified electrician or HVAC technician looking to move away from a traditional tools‑based role and into operations, or someone earlier in their technical career who is curious about how large‑scale, mission‑critical environments operate.

Regardless of background, we value motivation, strong attention to detail, and a willingness to learn and develop within a growing industry.

Desirable experience:

  • A trade or technical background in Electrical, Refrigeration/HVAC, Mechanical, or a related field (highly desirable)
  • Experience working in critical or high‑availability environments with strong safety and compliance requirements
  • Exposure to monitoring or control systems such as BMS, EMS, or SCADA‑type platforms
  • Familiarity with complex infrastructure or plant equipment (e.g. HVAC systems, power systems, generators, fire systems)
  • Strong fault‑finding, problem‑solving, and situational awareness skills
  • The ability to produce clear documentation, logs, and post‑incident reports

Australian Citizenship with ability to obtain and maintain a NV1 Security Clearance.

About us

Established in 2007, CDC Data Centres is Australia’s leading operator of sovereign, secure, world-class data centre facilities.

Headquartered in Canberra with multiple facilities in the ACT, NSW, VIC and New Zealand, CDC’s diversified operations provide secure data centre configurations that support co-location, containerised and hyperscale compute environments with all campuses interconnected with high-speed carrier grade networks.

At CDC we are passionate about creating an inclusive workplace that promotes and values diversity. We believe that everyone’s unique experiences enable us to deliver meaningful benefits for our people, our clients and communities. Our mission is to attract, retain and grow the world’s best data centre team.

Our people are committed, tenacious and meticulous in supporting our customers. Together, we configure the landscape to meet the security, reliability, connectivity and sustainability needs for today and tomorrow.

About the role

**The Associate Service Technician 24/7 position is a vital role that significantly contributes to the continuity and efficiency of our Data Centre Operations teams. The Associate Service Technician role is designed to uphold the highest standards of operational excellence and to ensure the continued customer satisfaction and data centre uptime we are known for. This role encompasses supporting customers, maintenance and monitoring activities, and is a key role in CDC’s career pathways initiative with investment in learning and development opportunities, as we empower our teams for future growth.

Other responsibilities include:

  • Support and engage with Customers, Service Technicians and contractors undertaking support activities and overseeing maintenance works.
  • Monitor critical infrastructure to ensure continuity of services and no disruption to client’s or business operations.
  • Utilise electronic monitoring systems to proactively oversee and monitor site conditions.
  • Respond to customer requests and critical events swiftly,
  • Ensure personnel are performing activities safely and in accordance with CDC’s processes and procedures.
  • Provide timely reporting of events, and support restoration to normal operations.

What’s in it for you:

CDC offers excellent employment conditions and benefits such as:

  • CDC Academy -Mark your mark by enhancing your professional development with the CDC Academy. Enrol in specialised training courses that will help you develop skills and ensure you thrive in your chosen career.
  • CDC Day - An additional day of paid leave dedicated to nurturing your health and wellbeing.
  • Parental Leave - Inclusive and above legislative tenure of parental leave entitlements to help you start, grow and care for your family.

  • CDC Social Events - CDC’s offers staff and their family’s inclusive events that nurtures relationships, connection and friendships across the business. CDC hosts BBQs, family picnics and community events, bringing together CDC staff in different settings.

About you

Whether you’ve recently completed your trade or you’re someone without a trade qualification but motivated to learn and grow, this role offers an excellent entry point into CDC’s rapid expansion. It’s a strong opportunity to step into the data centre industry, with genuine room to develop and progress your career.

You will also bring:

Essential:

Australian Citizenship with ability to obtain and maintain a NV1 Security Clearance.

How to Apply:

If you are looking for an opportunity to play a vital role in a fast-growing Australian Technology company and be part of our amazing team, please submit your resume and cover letter by clicking Apply.

We are committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive workplace where all individuals are valued and respected. We believe that diversity of backgrounds, perspectives, and experiences leads to innovation and success. We actively promote equality and strive to create a welcoming environment for all employees. We are dedicated to building a team that reflects the diversity of our community and we encourage everyone to bring their authentic selves to work.

job.title: Director - ICT Engineering (APAC)
job.description:
Company Overview

STACK Infrastructure builds, owns, and operates hyperscale and colocation data centers that power the world’s most ambitious technology companies. With a rapidly expanding footprint across APAC, STACK combines deep development expertise, flexible capital, and operational discipline to deliver critical digital infrastructure at scale.

Our clients include the largest hyperscale cloud platforms. We are building a regional platform defined by speed of delivery, power reliability, and long-term partnership — and we are assembling the team to lead that effort.

The Position:

STACK leads with culture and provides a flexible working environment focused on productivity and goals.

As STACK rapidly grows throughout the region, our ICT Engineering Team is growing in response to the increased number of projects and sites under development. As part of this growth, we seek an energetic and focused individual to join our APAC Team to provide support in the ICT design, delivery, and operational management of our data centers. Leads in all ICT matters and supporting our in-country project team in developing data center ICT designs for OT systems and maintaining accurate ICT project timelines, mapping concurrent and sequential project activities, critical path, identifying key resource (internal and external) throughout each stage of the project delivery. This also includes identifying ICT managed service providers and managing them to meet day-to-day operational uptime requirements. While reporting to the regional APAC team, you will be working in a flat team structure surrounded by industry leaders across all aspects of Data Centre and Real Estate Development.

In this role you will:

Leadership and Team Management

  • Lead and develop the OT/ICT design team, including engineers, architects, system administrators and specialists.
  • Establish the team structure, roles, responsibilities and technical governance required to support multiple concurrent projects.
  • Develop workforce and resource plans based on the project pipeline, design workload and delivery priorities.
  • Allocate internal and external resources across projects while managing capacity constraints and competing deadlines.
  • Set team objectives, performance expectations and professional-development plans.
  • Build technical capability in OT networking, ICT infrastructure, systems integration, cybersecurity and data-centre technology.

Data Center ICT Design Management

  • Take overall accountability for the quality, completeness and timely delivery of OT and ICT designs.
  • Covers all technology requirements, not limited to computing, network, cybersecurity technologies
  • Define and maintain standard design requirements, technical specifications, reference architectures and approved product standards.
  • Ensure designs are scalable, resilient, maintainable, secure and aligned with operational requirements.
  • Oversee Data Center ICT and industrial networks, structured cabling and fibre, LAN/WAN connectivity, and BMS/EPMS/Scada, Dcim, Security & CCTV integration, wireless access points, NMS monitoring and OT remote-access solutions.
  • Chair technical design reviews and ensure design issues, interfaces and risks are identified, assigned and resolved.
  • Manage design changes and deviations from approved standards, and review with VP, Operational Technology as required.
  • Ensure technical documentation, drawings, equipment schedules, interface matrices and commissioning requirements are complete and properly controlled.

Project Planning and Delivery Coordination

  • Work with project directors, delivery managers, construction teams and commissioning teams to develop realistic OT/ICT delivery plans. This includes planning for telco and internet service providers.
  • Translate project milestones into design, procurement, installation, integration, testing and commissioning activities.
  • Identify long-lead equipment and critical technology packages early and incorporate them into procurement plans.
  • Identify resource needs and ensure the correct technical expertise is available at each project stage.
  • Monitor design progress against the master project schedule and implement recovery plans where necessary.
  • Manage dependencies between OT/ICT systems and electrical, mechanical, security, architectural and operational workstreams.
  • Resolve technical issues that could affect project cost, programme, quality or commissioning.
  • Support project readiness reviews, integrated systems testing, handover and operational acceptance.

Vendor and Supplier Management

  • Develop and maintain strategic relationships with equipment manufacturers, technology vendors, suppliers, Internet Service providers, consultants and system integrators.
  • Establish technical qualification and approval processes for vendors and products.
  • Participate in tender preparation, technical bid evaluation, vendor selection and contract negotiations.
  • Define clear scopes of work, technical deliverables, service levels and acceptance criteria.
  • Monitor vendor performance in relation to quality, cost, schedule, technical compliance and responsiveness.
  • Conduct regular vendor performance and technology-roadmap reviews.
  • Manage supplier-related risks, including product obsolescence, cybersecurity vulnerabilities, capacity constraints and long lead times.
  • Work with procurement and commercial teams to develop strategic sourcing and framework agreements while avoiding unnecessary vendor lock-in.

Technical Governance and Assurance

  • Establish governance processes for design reviews, technical approvals, deviations and change control.
  • Ensure compliance with corporate policies, customer requirements, contractual obligations and applicable standards.
  • Maintain clear segregation and controlled integration between enterprise ICT and operational technology environments.
  • Ensure designs incorporate availability, redundancy, maintainability and disaster-recovery requirements.
  • Coordinate with cybersecurity teams so security requirements are embedded throughout the design and delivery lifecycle.
  • Oversee off site staging planning, site acceptance testing and integrated systems testing.
  • Ensure lessons learned from completed projects are incorporated into future design standards.

Budget, Commercial and Stake Holder Management

  • Prepare and manage the OT/ICT design and professional services budget.
  • Support capital-cost planning and cost benchmarking for OT/ICT systems.
  • Review project estimates, vendor proposals, variations and value-engineering opportunities.
  • Balance capital expenditure with reliability, lifecycle cost, operational efficiency and technology risk.
  • Provide accurate forecasts for internal resources, consultants, software licenses, equipment and support services.
  • Act as the senior technical interface between design, delivery, operations, procurement, cybersecurity and corporate ICT teams.
  • Communicate technical risks, resource constraints and program impacts clearly to senior leadership.
  • Engage operational teams early so systems can be supported, maintained and operated effectively after handover.
  • Represent the organization in technical meetings with customers, partners, consultants and suppliers.
  • Build alignment across regional teams while maintaining consistent APAC standards.

Key Details:

Location: Asia Pacific region

Travel: 20-30%

Language: English (Written, Spoken and Reading); Chinese (Spoken and Reading) Additional Regional Languages considered an advantage.

Must-have Qualifications:

  • Degree in information technology, telecommunications, electrical engineering, computer engineering, control systems or a related discipline.
  • Typically, 12-15 years of experience in OT, ICT, systems engineering or technology infrastructure.
  • At least five years in a senior leadership or design-management position.
  • Demonstrated experience managing multidisciplinary design teams and multiple concurrent projects.
  • Strong experience in mission-critical facilities, preferably data centers.
  • Proven ability to coordinate design, procurement, construction, testing and commissioning activities against complex project schedules.
  • Experience managing vendors, consultants, equipment manufacturers and system integrators.
  • Working knowledge of OT cybersecurity, network architecture, structured cabling, systems integration and operational monitoring platforms.
  • Experience with project planning, resource forecasting, budgeting and commercial evaluation.
  • Relevant professional certifications - such as PMP, CISSP, CISM, CCNP, TOGAF, ITIL or Chartered Engineer status - would be advantageous.
  • Excellent communication and troubleshooting skills.
  • Excellent documentation skills & working within an ITSM toolset.
  • Strong technical background with Cisco Certification for Networking Systems (CCNP or higher).
  • Good knowledge in firewalls and configurations for Palo Alto and Fortinet as a minimum.
  • Excellent in Cisco SDA architecture, Catalysis and Meraki product line from Cisco.
  • Experienced in the following key tools – Azure/Microsoft Entra ID cloud service knowledge.
  • Experience working with Telco and service providers.
  • Knowledge of Virtualization technology (VMWare) and servers will be an added advantage.
  • Self-driven, results-oriented with a positive outlook, and a clear focus on high quality and business goals.
  • A forward planner who can work independently to identify and resolve project issues.

This might be right for you if:

  • Are passionate about project controls and optimization, process focused with a deep understanding for Development / Construction Project Scheduling.
  • You don’t get flustered easily. You can juggle multiple high-level priorities with competing timelines while welcoming a new, urgent challenge with ease.
  • Are culturally sensitive and enjoy working across different markets in APAC.
  • You pay attention to the details – meticulously, and every time. Nothing falls through the cracks on your watch.
  • You’re collaborative. You enjoy working with others to solve problems – and people enjoy working with you.
  • You’re smart. You think five steps ahead and see issues from multiple angles. You’re not just a problem solver – you’re a problem preventer.
  • Have a strong desire to learn and develop within a new and fast paced industry.
  • High organizational skill set / mind set.

Why STACK:

  • We offer a competitive compensation package with strong benefits.
  • We have a culture of appreciation and recognition.
  • We are passionate about what we do and have fun doing it.
  • Be part of the growing business and make an impact.

STACK is an Equal Opportunity Employer. ALL qualified applications will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity and expression, age, national origin, mental or physical disability, genetic information, veteran status, or any other status protected by law.

job.title: Critical Operations Technician - Electrical (Australia)
job.description:
Company Overview

STACK Infrastructure builds, owns, and operates hyperscale and colocation data centers that power the world’s most ambitious technology companies. With a rapidly expanding footprint across APAC, STACK combines deep development expertise, flexible capital, and operational discipline to deliver critical digital infrastructure at scale.

Our clients include the largest hyperscale cloud platforms. We are building a regional platform defined by speed of delivery, power reliability, and long-term partnership — and we are assembling the team to lead that effort.

Summary/Objective

The Critical Operations Technician provides 24×7×365 operational coverage to support continuous, safe and reliable performance of critical electrical, mechanical, cooling, controls and life-safety systems across the data centre. The role performs hands-on operational maintenance, system monitoring, first-response troubleshooting, incident support and contractor coordination to uphold STACK’s 100% uptime commitment. Technicians operate and monitor facility infrastructure across power and cooling paths within approved procedures and role-specific authorisations, while maintaining a concierge-level customer service approach in all stakeholder interactions.

Essential Functions – Critical Operations

  • Maintain 24×7×365 shift coverage, ensuring safe and stable operation of all critical infrastructure systems.
  • Operate and monitor critical electrical and/or mechanical systems (based on background, training and authorisation) including UPS, PDUs, switchboards, generators, CDU/FWU/CRAC/CRAH units, chilled water systems, pumps and associated plant—strictly within approved operating procedures.
  • Perform hands-on operational maintenance within authorised scope, including inspections, condition monitoring, equipment resets, minor adjustments and component-level replacements (non-licenced work).
  • Identify abnormal conditions, complete initial diagnostics, implement first-level rectification actions where authorised, and escalate promptly to the Senior Data Centre Specialist.
  • Respond to alarms and operational incidents, supporting containment, investigation, communication and restoration activities.
  • Use BMS/EPMS and monitoring platforms to track alarms, interpret trends and support performance optimisation within approved limits.
  • Complete structured rounds including meter readings, thermal/capacity checks and condition observations, recording findings accurately.
  • Coordinate and supervise licenced contractors performing trade-restricted works, ensuring compliance with permits, LOTO and site safety requirements.
  • Support planned maintenance, shutdowns, testing and return-to-service activities through operational tasks, witnessing and verification.
  • Maintain accurate shift logs, event records, handover notes and CMMS updates to ensure full operational traceability.
  • Proactively identify and report reliability risks and improvement opportunities to support STACK’s 100% uptime commitment.
  • Participate in incident management training and exercises, acting as a trained first responder under direction of incident leaders.
  • Contribute to continuous improvement of SOPs, MOPs, EOPs, risk assessments and operational readiness activities.
  • Provide professional, timely communication to customers and stakeholders to support a high-quality service experience.
  • This role does not perform licenced electrical, mechanical or refrigeration work. All trade-restricted activities are undertaken by appropriately qualified contractors or licenced personnel. The role focuses on operational system management, first-response troubleshooting, vendor coordination and component-level maintenance within authorised limits.

People

  • Set a high standard for safety behaviour, operational discipline and professional conduct across the shift.
  • Support technicians through on-the-job coaching, demonstrations and constructive feedback to improve capability and consistency.
  • Assist with onboarding and familiarisation of new team members, reinforcing authorised boundaries and operational expectations.
  • Strengthen team communication by ensuring clear handovers, accurate escalation details and calm coordination during events.
  • Participate actively in briefings, toolbox talks, training and operational discussions, offering practical observations and improvement ideas.
  • Build collaborative relationships with Security, Projects and vendor personnel to support safe, coordinated site operations.
  • Demonstrate a concierge‑level customer service approach in all interactions with customers, visitors and stakeholders.

Competencies

  • Operational discipline with a strong focus on safety, risk control and reliability
  • Ability to operate critical electrical and/or mechanical systems within procedural and authorisation boundaries
  • Effective troubleshooting, root-cause thinking and first-response decision-making under pressure
  • Ability to interpret alarms, trends and technical documentation (SLDs, O&M manuals, procedures)
  • Proficient in digital operational systems (BMS/EPMS, CMMS, workflow platforms) and reporting tools
  • Strong communication skills and calm, structured incident support
  • Contractor coordination capability with sound permit-to-work and LOTO awareness
  • Customer-focused, professional service orientation
  • Collaborative team behaviour with personal accountability and consistency on shift
  • Continuous improvement approach (procedures, logs, risk reduction and operational uplift)

Preferred Education and Experience

  • 2-3 years' experience in critical environments such as data centres, hospitals, utilities, defence, industrial plants or similar operational settings.
  • Demonstrated capability operating and/or monitoring electrical and/or mechanical infrastructure (e.g., UPS, generators, switchgear, PDUs/PMMs, ATS/STS, CRAC/CRAH, chilled water systems, pumps, fire systems and controls).
  • Hands-on experience performing operational maintenance and first-level rectification activities within authorised limits.
  • Experience using BMS/EPMS and CMMS/workflow tools to manage alarms, work orders and operational documentation.
  • Ability to interpret technical drawings and documentation (including single-line diagrams and O&M manuals).
  • Familiarity with permit-to-work, LOTO and basic risk assessment principles.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills suitable for shift logs, incident updates and customer/stakeholder engagement.

Work Environment/Conditions

  • Role operates on a 24×7 rotating shift roster including nights, weekends and public holidays.
  • Work occurs in data halls, plant rooms, electrical/mechanical spaces and external plant areas; PPE is required as per site policy.
  • Participation in emergency response activities and incident exercises is required.

Work Authorization/Security Clearance Requirements

  • Legal entitlement to work in Australia.
  • Ability to satisfy pre-employment screening requirements (as applicable), including right-to-work checks, background checks and reference checks.
  • Ability to meet data centre security requirements including badging, access control and adherence to customer-mandated security protocols.
  • Security clearance is not required unless specified for a customer-specific facility.

Equal Opportunity Employer

STACK provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws.

This policy applies to all terms and conditions of employment, including recruiting, hiring, placement, promotion, termination, layoff, recall, transfer, leaves of absence, compensation, and training.

job.title: Electrical Network Coordinator (Australia)
job.description:
Company Overview

STACK Infrastructure builds, owns, and operates hyperscale and colocation data centers that power the world’s most ambitious technology companies. With a rapidly expanding footprint across APAC, STACK combines deep development expertise, flexible capital, and operational discipline to deliver critical digital infrastructure at scale.

Our clients include the largest hyperscale cloud platforms. We are building a regional platform defined by speed of delivery, power reliability, and long-term partnership — and we are assembling the team to lead that effort.

Summary/Objective

STACK is seeking an Electrical Network Coordinator to support the operation, maintenance and optimisation of the site-wide LV and HV electrical networks across the Truganina campus. As a key technical leader within the Critical Operations team, this role ensures safe, compliant and reliable operation of all electrical systems and contributes to the development and execution of engineering programs across LV/HV operations, safety, team performance, communication and knowledge.

The Electrical Network Coordinator plays a vital role in ensuring all mission-critical electrical infrastructure performs to the highest standards and remains fully compliant with customer SLAs, certifications and regulatory requirements.

This role directly supports STACK’s commitment to 100% uptime and a concierge-level customer service experience, ensuring risk is proactively managed, planned works are executed safely, and customer communications are clear, timely and professional.

Essential Functions

Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform these essential functions.

Operations

  • Foster and uphold a culture of working safely across all engineering operations.
  • Support LV and HV switching activities for delivery and operations across internal and external stakeholders.
  • Support compliance with Victorian Blue Book requirements and ensure processes conform to all regulatory obligations.
  • Execute all aspects of data centre operations, including operation, maintenance and repair of mission-critical electrical equipment, to ensure 100% uptime and compliance with customer SLAs and certifications.
  • Support Facilities Engineering team members to achieve high performance, including coaching and development.
  • Lead the development, implementation and auditing of MOPs, SOPs and EOPs aligned with STACK and industry best practice.

  • Communicate clearly and transparently, ensuring teams remain informed of relevant changes and operational decisions.

Competencies

Work Environment

Required Education and Experience

  • Strong knowledge of metering, remote switching, digital controls and BMS.
  • Effective communication and customer interaction skills.
  • Strong project management, troubleshooting and organisational capabilities.
  • Understanding of local and national regulatory codes and permit processes.

  • Experience with power quality analysis and protection coordination reviews.

Additional Eligibility Requirements

  • Willingness to work outside standard business hours, including weekends, nights and public holidays, and participate in an on-call roster.

Equal Opportunity Employer

job.title: Senior Critical Operations Manager (Australia)
job.description:
Company Overview

STACK Infrastructure builds, owns, and operates hyperscale and colocation data centers that power the world’s most ambitious technology companies. With a rapidly expanding footprint across APAC, STACK combines deep development expertise, flexible capital, and operational discipline to deliver critical digital infrastructure at scale.

Our clients include the largest hyperscale cloud platforms. We are building a regional platform defined by speed of delivery, power reliability, and long-term partnership — and we are assembling the team to lead that effort.

Summary/Objective

The Senior Critical Operations Manager is the senior operational leader for the data centre campus, responsible for the day-to-day performance, safety and reliability of all mission-critical operations. Reporting to the Site Director, this role oversees the Critical Operations Manager, Assistant Critical Operations Manager, and the Facilities Management team including the 24/7 workforce to ensure consistent, safe and resilient operation of all critical infrastructure.

The Senior Critical Operations Manager is accountable for driving operational excellence across all shifts, leading incident and risk management, and uplifting and maintaining operational processes, procedures, policies and document control. The role will participate in, and at times lead, operational readiness activities in partnership with the Readiness/Operational Projects function.

This role directly supports STACK’s commitment to 100% uptime and a concierge-level customer service experience, ensuring risk is proactively managed, planned works are executed safely, and customer communications are clear, timely and professional.

Acting as the Site Director’s primary operational delegate, the Senior Critical Operations Manager provides leadership continuity, clear communication, and consistent execution of operational standards across the site.

Essential Functions

Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform these essential functions.

Critical Operations Leadership

  • Set the operational tone for the campus and embed a safety-first culture across all shifts, contractors and stakeholders.
  • Provide day-to-day leadership to COM, ACOM, FM and 24/7 technical teams to ensure consistent, safe and resilient operations.
  • Ensure the 24/7 performance of all mechanical, electrical, fire life safety and control systems to maintain uninterrupted service and meet all SLAs, certifications and legislative requirements.
  • Act as the Site Director’s operational delegate when required, ensuring continuity of decision-making, escalation management and customer communication.

Incident, Risk and Change Governance

  • Lead incident management and problem management end-to-end, including escalation, risk-based decision-making, customer and executive communications, and the quality of PIR/RCA outputs through to corrective action closure.
  • Maintain the site risk register, hazard identification processes and risk review cadence, ensuring risks are visible, owned and mitigated.
  • Govern change control for planned works and live-site interventions, ensuring appropriate outage windows, hold points, rollback strategies and customer approvals.

Maintenance and Planned Works

  • Oversee maintenance planning and execution, including review and approval of MOPs, SOPs and EOPs, permit-to-work processes, isolations/LOTO, SWMS and vendor method statements.
  • Own scheduling and prioritisation of planned works and minor/medium projects, resolving conflicts across customer commitments, risk and operational constraints.
  • Ensure accurate and timely operational reporting on availability, incidents, risks, maintenance compliance, planned works and action tracking.

Contractor and Vendor Management

  • Provide governance and quality oversight of contractor and vendor activities, including safety leadership, performance management, service reviews and continuous improvement actions.
  • Ensure service partners remain aligned to STACK standards, scope and behaviours, and are held accountable to KPIs and SLAs.

Operational Readiness and Continuous Improvement

  • Uplift, implement and maintain operational processes, procedures, policies and document control to drive standardisation, audit readiness and continuous improvement across all shifts.
  • Ensure operational readiness requirements are met for new systems, upgrades and transitions (documentation, asset registers, CMMS updates, spares, tooling and training).
  • Provide oversight of operational projects impacting live operations, ensuring safe execution, quality outcomes and compliance with operational standards.

Customer Engagement and Communication

  • Act as a senior operational contact for customers, hosting forums, presenting updates, coordinating planned works communications and maintaining confidence during incidents.
  • Ensure communications are clear, timely and accurate across internal stakeholders, customers and leadership.

People and Culture

  • Set clear expectations and performance standards for COM, ACOM, FM and 24/7 teams, aligned to STACK values and behaviours.
  • Coach, mentor and develop team capability across all shifts, including succession planning, training coverage and role readiness.
  • Drive effective cross-shift communication and structured handovers to ensure alignment on priorities and consistent execution.

Competencies

  • 7-10 years’ leadership in mission-critical operations with demonstrated ownership of 24/7 environments.
  • Strong technical understanding of electrical, mechanical, fire life safety and control systems in data centres or equivalent critical facilities.
  • Proven incident leadership, including high-quality PIR/RCA delivery and action close-out.
  • Deep governance across maintenance planning, change control, permit-to-work, risk assessments and method statement review.
  • High customer service capability; confident presenting operational updates and managing planned works communications.
  • Strong contractor and vendor management capability with a focus on safety, performance and continuous improvement.
  • Competent with CMMS, monitoring platforms and incident/change/problem management systems.
  • Excellent organisation, prioritisation and decision-making across competing live-site demands.
  • Advanced written and verbal communication skills suitable for executive and customer audiences.

Work Environment / Conditions

Working onsite at STACK Data Centres in Victoria, Australia, including plant rooms, equipment spaces and live operating environments.

Travel Required

  • Minimal routine travel; occasional travel between local STACK facilities as operational needs require.
  • Occasional interstate or international travel may be required.

Required Education and Experience

  • Significant experience leading multidisciplinary technical teams in data centres or other mission-critical environments with 24/7 operations.
  • Demonstrated track record managing incidents, risks, maintenance and planned works in live environments.
  • Proficiency in operational reporting, stakeholder communication and customer engagement.
  • Strong working knowledge of CMMS, monitoring and incident/change/problem management systems.
  • High competency with Microsoft 365 (Outlook, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Teams).

Preferred Education and Experience

  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent professional experience.
  • Technical certifications or trade qualifications in electrical, mechanical, controls or related fields.
  • Experience contributing to operational readiness for new systems and major upgrades.
  • Experience with vendor performance management, KPI/SLA governance and contract service reviews.

Additional Eligibility Requirements

  • Willingness to work outside standard business hours, including weekends, public holidays, nights and on-call coverage as required.
  • Comfortable working in a fast-paced, high-pressure environment with shifting priorities.
  • Ongoing compliance with STACK policies, procedures and behavioural standards.

job.title: Contract & Cost Manager (Australia)
job.description:
Company Overview

STACK Infrastructure builds, owns, and operates hyperscale and colocation data centers that power the world’s most ambitious technology companies. With a rapidly expanding footprint across APAC, STACK combines deep development expertise, flexible capital, and operational discipline to deliver critical digital infrastructure at scale.

Our clients include the largest hyperscale cloud platforms. We are building a regional platform defined by speed of delivery, power reliability, and long-term partnership — and we are assembling the team to lead that effort.

Summary/Objective

The Contract & Cost Manager is responsible for the commercial administration, cost control and performance oversight of a substantial portfolio of operational contracts across STACK's Australian data centres. The assigned portfolio may represent material annual expenditure across engineering maintenance, facilities management, security, cleaning, utilities support and other critical operational services.

This role directly supports STACK’s commitment to 100% uptime and a concierge-level customer service experience, ensuring risk is proactively managed, planned works are executed safely, and customer communications are clear, timely and professional.

Reporting to the Senior Contract & Cost Manager, the role independently owns and administers a significant allocated portfolio and provides portfolio-level commercial governance throughout the procurement and contract lifecycle. This includes sourcing strategy, tendering, negotiation, contract execution, forecasting, payment assessment, variations, claims, vendor performance, renewals, transition and contract close-out.

The role is accountable for maintaining accurate visibility of contractual commitments, expenditure, financial risks and supplier performance; ensuring contracts remain within approved authority, value and term; and providing commercially sound recommendations to Operations and senior leadership. The Senior Contract & Cost Manager retains overall portfolio accountability.

Essential Functions

Reasonable adjustments may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform these essential functions.

Contract and Procurement Management

  • Independently own the commercial governance and day-to-day administration of the assigned operational contract portfolio.
  • Develop procurement and sourcing strategies and lead commercial procurement workstreams from market engagement through contract award.
  • Chair or lead the commercial component of tender evaluations, including bid analysis, clarifications, risk assessment, negotiation strategy and recommendation for approval.
  • Prepare clear commercial recommendations, approval papers and decision records for Operations and senior leadership.
  • Lead contract negotiations, drafting, execution, extensions, renewals, variations, terminations and close-out activities.
  • Administer contractual claims, including extension-of-time and delay claims, and assess entitlement, quantum, evidence and commercial risk.
  • Manage contractual notices, correspondence, records and governance requirements to preserve STACK's rights and ensure supplier obligations are enforceable.
  • Assess and apply performance deductions, service credits and liquidated damages where contractually applicable.
  • Lead dispute avoidance and support timely, commercially sound resolution of contractual disputes and claims.
  • Ensure insurance, indemnity, liability, security and other contractual risk requirements are established, maintained and verified.
  • Oversee contract mobilisation, transition, demobilisation and exit planning to protect service continuity and operational resilience.
  • Monitor supplier financial health, dependency and concentration risk, and recommend appropriate mitigation actions.
  • Ensure contracts do not expire, exceed approved authority or continue without appropriate contractual coverage and approvals.
  • Escalate material financial, contractual, supplier and delivery risks to the Senior Contract & Cost Manager and senior leadership with recommended actions.

Cost Management and Reporting

  • Lead annual budget development for the assigned portfolio and maintain accurate periodic reforecasts based on commitments, operational plans and emerging risks.
  • Prepare and validate monthly accruals, commitments, forecasts and variance analysis in coordination with Finance and Operations.
  • Maintain accurate reconciliation of contracted value, approved variations, purchase-order value, invoiced amounts and actual spend.
  • Assess payment claims and invoices against contractual entitlement, performance evidence, milestones, rates and approved purchase orders.
  • Maintain forward visibility of committed and forecast expenditure, including uncommitted requirements and anticipated changes.
  • Ensure compliance with delegated-authority limits, procurement controls, approval pathways and financial governance requirements.
  • Track, validate and report realised savings, negotiated benefits and cost avoidance without compromising safety, compliance or service quality.
  • Support financial audits, contract assurance reviews and internal control testing, and ensure timely closure of identified actions.
  • Undertake whole-of-life cost analysis and scenario modelling to inform sourcing, renewal and investment decisions.
  • Establish, monitor and report appropriate contingency and risk allowances for material contracts and procurement activities.
  • Prevent retrospective purchase orders, unapproved expenditure and services being delivered without valid contractual and financial authority.
  • Provide accurate portfolio-level cost reports, dashboards and commercial insights to the Senior Contract & Cost Manager, Operations, Finance and senior leadership.

Vendor Performance, Process and Continuous Improvement

  • Monitor contract progress and vendor performance against contractual obligations, maintenance requirements, key performance indicators and service-level agreements.
  • Develop and maintain a consistent vendor performance matrix across all data centres, supported by reliable evidence, trends and agreed improvement actions.
  • Lead or support formal supplier performance reviews, corrective-action plans and escalation processes for persistent or material underperformance.
  • Coach Operations Managers and other stakeholders in contract administration, commercial decision-making, record keeping and compliance with procurement controls.
  • Direct and coordinate consultants, quantity surveyors, contract administrators and other commercial resources engaged to support the assigned portfolio.
  • Manage, mentor or allocate work to junior commercial resources where required, ensuring appropriate quality control and capability development.
  • Present portfolio performance, risks, forecasts and commercial recommendations to executive and senior leadership forums.
  • Develop and maintain effective, standardised and streamlined commercial processes, procedures, templates and reporting tools.
  • Support innovation, initiatives and continuous improvement aimed at increasing the time, cost and operational efficiency of data centre operations.
  • Support multiple sites, including procurement and commercial preparations for new data centre capacity, operational transitions and capital improvement programs associated with existing data centres.

Competencies

  • Strong commercial judgement and a comprehensive understanding of contract management, administration and cost control.
  • Strong communication, negotiation, contract drafting and presentation skills, including the ability to communicate complex commercial matters clearly to executives and operational stakeholders.
  • Demonstrated ability to lead procurement workstreams, chair commercial evaluations and influence multiple internal and external stakeholders.
  • Strong financial analysis, forecasting and reporting capability, with the ability to identify trends, exposure and control weaknesses.
  • Good leadership, coaching, decision-making and problem-solving skills.
  • Ability to manage competing priorities and exercise sound judgement in a fast-paced, operationally critical environment.
  • Excellent attention to detail, record keeping and commitment to commercial integrity and governance.

Work Environment / Conditions

  • Based on-site at STACK's Melbourne data centres in Truganina, Melbourne.
  • The role operates in an active critical-infrastructure environment and requires close collaboration with site Operations, Engineering, Finance, Procurement, Legal and external service providers.

Travel Required

  • Travel between STACK data centre sites and the Melbourne head office may be required from time to time.
  • Travel to other STACK data centre facilities within Australia and internationally may be required from time to time.

Required Education and Experience

  • Minimum seven years' experience in commercial management, contract management, quantity surveying, procurement or cost management within operations, facilities management, engineering or critical infrastructure, with depth of experience appropriate to a substantial and complex portfolio.
  • Demonstrated responsibility for independently managing or commercially administering a significant annual contract portfolio with material organisational and operational impact.
  • Experience negotiating and administering complex, high-value facilities, maintenance, engineering or service contracts through the full contract lifecycle.
  • Demonstrated experience across maintenance, facilities management, engineering services and critical infrastructure environments.
  • Demonstrated experience in sourcing strategy, tendering, contract drafting, payment assessment, variations, forecasting, claims management, dispute resolution, renewals and vendor performance.
  • Demonstrated experience leading procurement workstreams, preparing commercial recommendations and presenting material risks and decisions to senior stakeholders.
  • Strong working knowledge of commercial governance, delegated authority, procurement controls, contractual risk and financial reporting.
  • Relevant tertiary qualification in quantity surveying, construction management, commercial management, engineering, finance, law or a related discipline.
  • Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel and experience with enterprise resource planning and financial platforms such as Oracle NetSuite.

Preferred Education and Experience

  • Experience working in a data centre or other critical-environment industry.
  • Experience managing large-scale facilities, maintenance or engineering-service contracts within a complex operational portfolio.
  • Experience with multi-site portfolios, supplier mobilisation and transition, service continuity planning and contract exit arrangements.
  • Experience directing consultants, contract administrators or junior commercial resources.

Equal Opportunity Employer

STACK provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, colour, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state or local laws.

job.title: Security and Compliance Manager (Australia)
job.description:
Company Overview

STACK Infrastructure builds, owns, and operates hyperscale and colocation data centers that power the world’s most ambitious technology companies. With a rapidly expanding footprint across APAC, STACK combines deep development expertise, flexible capital, and operational discipline to deliver critical digital infrastructure at scale.

Our clients include the largest hyperscale cloud platforms. We are building a regional platform defined by speed of delivery, power reliability, and long-term partnership — and we are assembling the team to lead that effort.

Summary/Objective

STACK is seeking a highly motivated, customer-focused security and compliance professional to provide hands-on policy and process support to the Critical Operations team and customers across STACK campuses.

The Security and Compliance Manager is responsible for day-to-day data centre security operations across STACK campuses, supporting and executing security projects and programs, assuring audit compliance with STACK and client policies and procedures, and responding to security incidents and operational escalations when required.

This role directly supports STACK’s commitment to 100% uptime and a concierge-level customer service experience, ensuring risk is proactively managed, planned works are executed safely, and customer communications are clear, timely and professional.

Essential Functions

Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform these essential functions.

Security Operations and Incident Management

  • Direct and manage contract guard force operations across STACK campuses.
  • Handle security incidents, escalations and other security-related issues across STACK campuses.
  • Participate in an after-hours on-call roster and provide management escalation support.
  • Respond to security incidents and emergency events across STACK campuses, including attending a campus outside standard business hours when required; ensure appropriate action is taken, reports are completed and relevant parties are notified in a timely manner.
  • Work closely with client security teams to deliver successful customer outcomes.
  • Troubleshoot physical security system performance issues and implement corrective actions.
  • Analyse physical security system performance and recommend improvements.
  • Collaborate with other teams to protect STACK personnel, information and assets.
  • Support the Senior Security and Compliance Manager in managing soft services.

Compliance, Policy, Training and Projects

  • Participate in recurring data centre security and compliance audits and reviews, including ISO 27001, SOC 1 and SOC 2, and PCI DSS.
  • Execute established compliance processes in accordance with STACK policies, standards and guidelines, and relevant legal and regulatory requirements.
  • Develop security methodologies, policies and procedures.
  • Conduct on-the-job training.
  • Prepare reports and communicate with management on the status of physical security operations and compliance.
  • Oversee new security construction and retrofit projects and manage the security handover process.
  • Ensure compliance with all work health and safety procedures and requirements, including permit to work, risk assessments, safe work method statements and personal protective equipment.

  • Comprehend, analyse and interpret complex documents.
  • Deliver effective presentations on data centre security and compliance to customers and management.
  • Respond effectively to sensitive issues, complex enquiries or complaints from security service providers, co-workers, supervisors and management.
  • Positively influence and motivate employees and Security Services Provider teams to achieve the required performance, placing team outcomes ahead of individual goals when necessary.

Security Services Provider Management

  • Foster and maintain positive working relationships with Security Services Providers, FM subcontractors, suppliers and consultants.
  • Assist the Senior Security and Compliance Manager in managing Security Services Providers engaged by STACK, including security guarding, off-site Security Alarm Monitoring Centre and locksmith providers, and oversee contract and service delivery against agreed KPIs and SLAs.
  • Review or prepare reports and information as required.
  • Assist with Security Services Provider meetings.
  • Regularly evaluate objectives and plans to support continual improvement and alignment of the Security Services Provider with STACK priorities.
  • Hold Security Services Provider team members accountable to performance standards and work with the provider to understand and address underperformance appropriately.

People and Collaboration

  • Operate in accordance with STACK values and contribute to a cohesive and positive working environment.
  • Establish and maintain close working relationships with stakeholders across STACK, FM Services Provider teams, joint venture partners, consortium members, consultants, contractors and suppliers.
  • Develop team members to maximise performance and realise their potential through coaching and mentoring.
  • Promote teamwork across the team, Security Services Provider and wider business.
  • Take accountability for achieving results aligned with STACK business goals.
  • Maintain open communication channels by keeping people informed of changes and decisions that affect them and ensuring relevant information is communicated promptly and accurately.
  • Participate in work-related team meetings and activities as required.

Work Environment / Conditions

Working on-site across STACK campuses in Melbourne.

Travel Required

Travel between STACK campuses and the STACK Melbourne head office may be required from time to time.

Travel to other STACK data centre facilities within Australia and internationally may be required from time to time.

Required Education and Experience

  • 5-7 years’ security operations experience.
  • At least three years’ experience in a leadership role.
  • Ability to analyse situations, make timely decisions and formulate action plans.
  • Demonstrated experience investigating security incidents and preparing detailed reports.
  • Demonstrated experience participating in an after-hours on-call roster and responding to security incidents and operational escalations, including outside standard business hours.
  • Experience working with security service providers.
  • Working knowledge of security software systems such as Gallagher, GENETEC, AMAG and Lenel.
  • Working knowledge of video surveillance equipment.
  • Familiarity with compliance standards such as ISO 27001 and SOC 2.
  • Proficiency with computers and Microsoft Office applications, including Outlook, Word, Excel and PowerPoint.
  • Capability to create and manage key performance metrics.
  • Experience training others in security procedures.
  • Ability to work independently with limited direction.

Preferred Education and Experience

  • Experience working in a high-security environment.
  • Conflict resolution training.
  • Ability to perform security risk assessments.
  • CPR/AED certification.
  • CPP or PSP certification.
  • Understanding of the Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF).
  • Certificate IV in Security Risk Management or equivalent.
  • Defence Security Officer training, or the ability to complete it.
  • Security Adviser Registration, or the ability to obtain it.
  • Security Officer licence, or the ability to obtain it.

Work Authorisation/Security Clearance Requirements

STACK Infrastructure builds, owns, and operates hyperscale and colocation data centers that power the world’s most ambitious technology companies. STACK is seeking an Electrical Network Coordinator to support the operation, maintenance and optimisation of the site-wide LV and HV electrical networks across the Truganina campus. As a key technical leader within the Critical Operations team, this role ensures safe, compliant and reliable operation of all electrical systems and contributes to the development and execution of engineering programs across LV/HV operations, safety, team performance, communication and knowledge.

The Electrical Network Coordinator plays a vital role in achieving STACK’s 100% uptime commitment, ensuring all mission-critical electrical infrastructure performs to the highest standards and remains fully compliant with customer SLAs, certifications and regulatory requirements. The role also upholds STACK’s concierge-level customer service, providing clear, confident and professional support when engaging with customers, partners and internal stakeholders.

Operations

  • Foster and uphold a culture of working safely across all engineering operations.

job.title: High Voltage Operations Manager (Australia)
job.description:

STACK Infrastructure builds, owns, and operates hyperscale and colocation data centers that power the world’s most ambitious technology companies. Summary/Objective

STACK is seeking an experienced High Voltage (HV) Operations Manager to lead the day-to-day delivery of high voltage operations across the Truganina campus. Reporting directly to Chief Engineer, this role will lead a team of Electrical Network Coordinators and ensure the safe, compliant and reliable operation of STACK’s HV electrical network.

This role directly supports STACK’s commitment to 100% uptime and a concierge-level customer service experience, ensuring risk is proactively managed, planned works are executed safely, and customer communications are clear, timely and professional.

The HV Operations Manager is accountable for coordinating daily switching activities, managing team workload and operational processes, and forecasting planned works to ensure the right resources, approvals and controls are in place. The successful candidate will bring a proven track record of people leadership, strong process discipline and the ability to manage multiple concurrent priorities within a mission-critical environment.

Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform these essential functions.

People Leadership and Team Management

  • Lead, coach and develop a team of Electrical Network Coordinators, setting clear expectations for safety, performance, accountability and collaboration.

HV Operations and Switching

Preferred Education and Experience

job.title: Critical Operations Director (Australia)
job.description:
Company Overview

STACK Infrastructure builds, owns, and operates hyperscale and colocation data centers that power the world’s most ambitious technology companies. With a rapidly expanding footprint across APAC, STACK combines deep development expertise, flexible capital, and operational discipline to deliver critical digital infrastructure at scale.

Our clients include the largest hyperscale cloud platforms. We are building a regional platform defined by speed of delivery, power reliability, and long-term partnership — and we are assembling the team to lead that effort.

Summary/Objective

STACK is seeking an experienced Critical Operations Director to establish and lead the Operations function for its Melbourne data centre campus. Reporting to the VP Critical Operations (Aust), this role has end-to-end accountability for site safety, operational readiness, reliability, customer service and the performance of all mission-critical mechanical, electrical, plumbing, fire life safety, controls and base-building systems.

This is a senior people leadership role for a proven leader who has successfully managed 100+ employees, including managers, supervisors and frontline technical teams. The Director will recruit, develop and lead the Operations team, work collaboratively across STACK, build trusted customer relationships and create an inclusive, accountable and high-performing culture. All Critical Operations staff report through this role.

Candidates may come from data centres or other complex mission-critical environments, including Defence, naval operations, aviation, utilities, power generation, transport, healthcare or large-scale industrial operations. Direct data-centre experience is advantageous but is not essential where the candidate can demonstrate leadership of large technical workforces, operational readiness, asset reliability and incident command in a high-consequence 24/7 environment.

This role directly supports STACK’s commitment to 100% uptime and a concierge-level customer service experience, ensuring risk is proactively managed, planned works are executed safely, and customer communications are clear, timely and professional.

Essential Functions

Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform these essential functions.

People Leadership and Team Performance

  • Provide visible, accountable and people-centred leadership for an operational workforce of 100+ employees across multiple shifts, technical disciplines and leadership levels.
  • Lead through managers and supervisors while remaining connected to frontline teams, setting clear priorities, modelling STACK values, ensuring consistent standards and maintaining effective escalation across every shift.
  • Build the campus Operations team from day one, owning workforce planning, recruitment, onboarding, retention, succession planning and development as the site ramps into full operation.
  • Set and actively manage performance expectations through regular leadership meetings, 1:1 sessions, coaching and talent reviews; ensure employees are trained and competent; recognise strong performance; and address performance issues promptly and consistently.
  • Create an inclusive, accountable and high-performing culture in which leaders collaborate, employees are empowered to make sound decisions and teams remain aligned to customer and operational priorities.

Operational Leadership and Reliability

  • Lead a standardised culture of always working safely and take full accountability for the readiness, uptime, reliability and day-to-day operation of the campus.
  • Provide credible technical leadership across mechanical, electrical and plumbing systems, fire life safety, controls and other mission-critical infrastructure.
  • Ensure preventive and predictive maintenance programs, technical procedures and critical work packages are executed safely through robust change management, protecting live operations during construction and commissioning.
  • Lead critical operational decisions and the response to abnormal conditions, incidents and emergencies, including customer communications, root-cause analysis and corrective action tracking.
  • Manage site systems, capacity and efficiency using CMMS, EPMS and BMS to avoid customer-impacting outages and support informed operational decisions.

Collaboration, Customer Service and Commercial Management

  • Work collaboratively with the VP Critical Operations (Aust) and across Engineering, Construction, Commissioning, Security, Commercial, Customer, Finance and Procurement to deliver coordinated outcomes for the campus.
  • Build trusted relationships with customers and act as the senior operational leader for the campus, providing clear, timely and professional communication on inquiries, planned work, incidents, risks and service performance.
  • Champion STACK’s concierge-level customer service, ensure the team understands customer contracts and SLAs, and resolve escalations with empathy, sound judgement and a solutions-focused approach.
  • Maintain clear, timely and professional customer communication before, during and after planned works, incidents and service-impacting events.
  • Manage vendor performance, service contracts, procurement, billing and compliance with agreed KPIs and SLAs.
  • Develop and manage site CAPEX and OPEX budgets, balancing reliability, safety, customer commitments and total cost of ownership.
  • Drive operational excellence through proactive planning, risk management, continuous improvement, site projects, reporting, audits and compliance activities; advise the VP Critical Operations (Aust) on performance, risks and priorities.
  • Maintain on-call availability and provide senior leadership during emergency situations or significant operational events.

Competencies

  • Proven senior people-management experience leading 100+ employees, including managers, supervisors and frontline technical staff in a complex 24/7 environment.
  • Proven ability to recruit, build, inspire and develop high-performing technical teams, with strong coaching, succession planning and performance-management capability.
  • Highly collaborative leadership style, with demonstrated success partnering across Operations, Engineering, Construction, Commissioning, Security, Commercial, Customer, Finance and Procurement to deliver coordinated outcomes.
  • Customer-focused leader with demonstrated ability to build trusted relationships, manage expectations, resolve escalations and deliver clear, timely and professional service.
  • Sufficient technical credibility to lead and challenge senior mechanical, electrical, controls, fire and facilities specialists. The successful candidate does not need to be the subject-matter expert in every discipline but must demonstrate sound technical judgement, disciplined risk management and the ability to make informed operational decisions.

Work Environment

  • Based on-site at Truganina Campus, Melbourne, with travel, on-call availability and work outside standard hours as required.

Required Education and Experience

  • Extensive experience leading operations within a live data centre, Defence environment or other high-consequence mission-critical operation, with accountability for a workforce of 100+ employees, operational readiness, safety, asset reliability and emergency response.
  • Proven record of recruiting, coaching, developing and retaining managers, supervisors and frontline technical teams, including succession planning and consistent performance management.
  • Demonstrated success working collaboratively across functions and influencing senior stakeholders to deliver coordinated operational outcomes.
  • Demonstrated customer-service leadership, including building trusted relationships and communicating clearly during planned works, incidents and service escalations.
  • Demonstrated experience managing maintenance, vendors, complex projects, customers and significant site budgets, with strong knowledge of service-level obligations, regulatory compliance and relevant building-code requirements. Direct experience with data centre SLAs is advantageous but not essential.

Preferred Education and Experience

  • Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Facilities Management, Business or a related discipline, or equivalent military, operational or professional experience.
  • Senior command, engineering, sustainment or operational leadership experience within the Australian Defence Force or an allied Defence organisation will be highly regarded.

Additional Eligibility Requirements

  • Willingness to work outside normal business hours, including weekends, public holidays and on-call support, in a high-pressure environment.

Work Authorisation/Security Clearance Requirements

  • Full Australian working rights and ability to pass background checks and attain and maintain NV1 security clearance where required.
